Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly IDD conduct-metric pack and its benchmark commentary for the EU/EEA distribution footprint; escalates every red metric to the Conduct Risk Committee and the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17(1) and Art. 30(3) plus Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 16 re-read on the EUR-Lex consolidated text at each quarter-end, alongside the current EIOPA Consumer Trends Report and EIOPA retail risk indicator definitions used as the external benchmark

In-scope processes.value: The quarterly conduct-metric cycle over all EU/EEA advised and non-advised distribution: complaints handling, cooling-off/free-look cancellations, 13-month persistency, replacement and switching, Art. 24 cross-selling attach rates, and inducement-to-premium ratios on insurance-based investment products

In-scope systems.value: Conduct Risk Dashboard in Power BI built over enterprise data warehouse feeds from the policy administration system, the complaints case tool and the commission platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metrics and Benchmarking Procedure — one row per metric giving formula, source table, data owner, amber/red tolerance, benchmark source (EIOPA Consumer Trends Report; NAIC MCAS peer ratios) and the escalation path for a breach

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Conduct Risk Committee; metric definitions and tolerances re-approved each January and re-opened whenever EIOPA republishes its retail risk indicators or the NAIC changes an MCAS ratio definition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Dashboard published within 20 business days of each quarter-end; the Q4 pack additionally feeds the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement due 30 April for the prior calendar year and the EIOPA Consumer Trends questionnaire returned to the national competent authority in Q3

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recurring tasks at quarter-end +5 business days (data cut frozen), +12 (metrics computed and reconciled), +20 (committee pack issued), raised for each of the four quarters plus a 1 March reminder for the MCAS feed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly metric pack, dated SQL extracts, benchmark source PDFs and Conduct Risk Committee minutes retained 5 years from publication, matching the IDD record-keeping expectation applied across EU/EEA branches

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every red metric opens a conduct issue carrying product, channel, country, root cause, owner and closure date; the issue only closes after two consecutive quarters inside tolerance

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the quarterly pack and personally closes each red-metric action once the metric has returned inside tolerance for two consecutive quarters

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every metric published in the quarterly Conduct Risk Dashboard for the tested quarter, together with the underlying complaint cases, policies in force, lapses, cooling-off cancellations and commission records that feed them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A metric fails if recomputation differs from the published value by more than 2%, if a red metric has no logged conduct issue, or if the benchmark comparison cites a superseded EIOPA or MCAS publication; two or more fails makes the quarter ineffective

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation runs quarterly, so the test runs quarterly on the just-published pack, with an annual four-quarter deep dive completed before the EIOPA Consumer Trends questionnaire is returned

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Market Conduct Compliance and must not have computed, sourced or commented on any metric in the pack under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly conduct-metric test workpaper — population extract, recomputation sheet, benchmark captures, exception list — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Conduct Monitoring / IDD Art. 17(1)

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Metric definitions, four quarters of dashboards, dated benchmark sources and committee minutes assembled as an Art. 17(1) conduct-governance response within 10 business days of a national competent authority request

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance drafts the response to the national competent authority or the lead US market conduct examiner; Regulatory Counsel clears any wording that concedes an adverse conduct trend before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Fix the conduct metric inventory for the quarter
actions: In the GRC platform open Conduct Risk ▸ Metric Library and filter Regulation = IDD (EU) 2016/97, Status = Active.

Confirm the library still carries the eleven mandatory rows: complaints per 1,000 policies in force, upheld-complaint rate, cooling-off cancellation rate within the 14-day Art. 186 window, 13-month lapse rate, replacement/switching rate, Art. 24 cross-sell attach rate, advised-versus-non-advised split, IBIP inducement-to-premium ratio, suitability-report issuance rate, claims declinature rate and vulnerable-customer complaint share.

For each row check formula, source table, data owner and amber/red tolerance are populated; where EIOPA has republished a retail risk indicator definition since last quarter, update the formula field and record the EIOPA publication date in the Source Reference field.
Email the metric owners in Complaints, Distribution and Commissions the frozen inventory with the quarter-end +5 data-cut date and keep the sent item.
Set the Metric Library version stamp to the quarter under measurement so the pack can be reproduced later.
checklist.done: the metric inventory is version-stamped for the quarter with every formula, tolerance and owner populated and circulated.

checklist.step: Extract the complaints population for the quarter
actions: In the complaints case tool run the saved query Complaints ▸ IDD Conduct Extract for the quarter, selecting case id, country of the policyholder, product, distribution channel, intermediary code, open date, close date, root-cause code and outcome (upheld / partly upheld / not upheld).
Filter to the EIOPA complaints-handling taxonomy categories that matter here: sales and advice, product information and disclosure, charges and value, and administration.
Reconcile the case count to the complaints register total for the quarter and explain any difference in writing before releasing the file.
Hand the extract to the Data Analyst as complaints-<quarter>.csv and copy the Consumer Affairs Manager so the narrative commentary can be prepared in parallel.
checklist.done: the complaints extract reconciles to the complaints register and is handed over with root-cause and outcome coding intact.

checklist.step: Extract the exposure denominators the ratios depend on
actions: Query the policy fact tables in the warehouse for policies in force at quarter-end, new business policies sold in the quarter, and gross written premium, split by country, product and distribution channel.

Pull cancellations flagged with a cooling-off/free-look reason code and cancellations outside that window as separate columns so the Art. 186 statutory 14-day withdrawal right can be measured on its own.
Pull lapses with policy duration in months so the 13-month early-lapse ratio can be computed on the correct cohort.
Reconcile policies in force and gross written premium to the quarter-end management accounts produced by Finance and record the reconciling items on the extract cover sheet.
Publish the denominators to the Conduct Monitoring schema and notify the BI Developer that the feed is ready.
checklist.done: denominators are published, split by country/product/channel, and reconciled to the quarter-end management accounts.

checklist.step: Compute the persistency, cancellation and replacement metrics
actions: Run the conduct metric notebook in Snowflake against the frozen quarter to compute the 13-month lapse rate as policies lapsing within 13 months of inception divided by policies incepted in the matching cohort.

Compute the cooling-off cancellation rate as cancellations inside the 14-day withdrawal window divided by new business policies sold, and the replacement rate as new policies flagged as replacing an existing in-force contract divided by new business policies.
Break every metric out by intermediary code so single-producer outliers do not vanish inside a country average.
Write the results into the CONDUCT_METRIC_QUARTER table with the metric id, value, numerator, denominator and the query hash so the number can be re-derived.
Send the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager a variance note on any metric that moved more than 20% against the prior quarter.
checklist.done: persistency, cooling-off and replacement metrics are stored with numerator, denominator and query hash, broken out by intermediary.

checklist.step: Compute the remuneration and inducement conduct metrics
actions: Extract from the commission platform, for the quarter, commission and non-monetary benefit amounts paid per intermediary per product, split first-year versus renewal.

Compute the IBIP inducement-to-premium ratio as total inducements paid on insurance-based investment products divided by premium written on those products, per country, so the Art. 29(2) quality test has a measured input.
Flag any intermediary whose first-year commission ratio exceeds twice the country median, and any product where the ratio moved more than 5 percentage points in the quarter.
Hand the flagged list to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and to the Suitability Desk reviewer who owns the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 8 inducement assessments.
Store the computation in the Conduct Monitoring schema with the commission run identifiers used.
checklist.done: inducement ratios are computed per country and product, outlier intermediaries are flagged and handed to the inducement assessment owner.

checklist.step: Compute the advice-quality metrics from suitability and demands-and-needs records
actions: In the CRM run the report Distribution ▸ Advice Quality ▸ IDD Quarter, counting sales with an advised flag, sales with a completed demands-and-needs statement, and IBIP sales with a suitability report issued under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 14.
Compute the suitability-report issuance rate as reports issued divided by advised IBIP sales, and the demands-and-needs completion rate as completed statements divided by all sales, both per country.

Compute the share of advised sales where the recorded sustainability preference in the profile does not match the product's SFDR classification, using the field added for Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1257.
Send the three rates plus the mismatch count to the Data Analyst for loading into CONDUCT_METRIC_QUARTER and copy the Sustainability Risk Manager on the sustainability mismatch figure.
checklist.done: advice-quality and sustainability-preference metrics are computed per country and loaded into the quarterly metric table.

checklist.step: Load the external benchmarks the metrics are measured against
actions: Download the current EIOPA Consumer Trends Report and the accompanying retail risk indicator annex from eiopa.europa.eu and save both to the regulatory library with their publication dates.
Download the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement peer ratio report from NAIC iSite+ ▸ MCAS ▸ Ratio Reports for the most recent data year for each line the company writes.

Build a benchmark table mapping each internal metric id to its external comparator, the comparator value, the source document and the source publication date; where no external comparator exists, record the internal three-year rolling median instead and label it as such.
Reject any comparator whose source publication is more than two years old and go back to the regulator site for the current edition.
Publish the benchmark table to the Conduct Monitoring schema and file the source PDFs beside it.
checklist.done: each metric has a dated external comparator (or a labelled internal median) with the source document filed.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly Conduct Risk Dashboard
actions: Refresh the Conduct Risk Dashboard dataset in Power BI against CONDUCT_METRIC_QUARTER and the benchmark table for the frozen quarter.
Render each metric with the quarter value, the prior four quarters, the external comparator and the amber/red tolerance band, with slicers for country, product and distribution channel.
Add a drill-through page that lists the underlying complaint cases or intermediary codes behind any metric a reader clicks, so a regulator question can be answered from the same screen.
Validate three metrics by hand against the Snowflake query output before publishing and record the tie-out in the refresh log.
Publish to the Conduct Risk workspace and grant read access to the Conduct Risk Committee distribution list only.
checklist.done: the dashboard is refreshed, drill-through works, three metrics are tied out by hand and access is restricted to the committee list.

checklist.step: Apply the tolerances and classify every metric green, amber or red
actions: Compare each metric to its amber and red tolerance in the Metric Library version stamped for the quarter, not to a remembered threshold.
Classify red where the metric breaches tolerance, or where it exceeds the EIOPA or MCAS comparator by more than the agreed margin, or where it has been amber for three consecutive quarters.
Write a one-paragraph rationale against every amber and red metric naming the country, product and channel driving it.
Where a metric moved because of a data change rather than a conduct change, state the data change and attach the Data Analyst's reconciliation note rather than reclassifying the metric quietly.
checklist.done: every metric carries a green/amber/red classification against the version-stamped tolerance with a written rationale for each amber and red.

checklist.step: Investigate each red metric down to root cause
actions: For each red metric pull the drill-through record list and read at least ten underlying cases, sales files or intermediary records end to end.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: sales-practice failure, product design or target-market mismatch, remuneration incentive, disclosure defect, servicing failure, or data-quality defect.
Interview the accountable Distribution Operations Manager or Broker Relationship Manager for the affected channel and minute the answer.

Where the cause is a sales-practice failure by a named intermediary, hand the intermediary code straight to the Producer Compliance Manager for immediate supervision action rather than waiting for the committee.
Record the root cause, evidence references and interviewees against the metric in the quarterly pack.
checklist.done: each red metric has a named root cause supported by at least ten inspected underlying records and a minuted business interview.

checklist.step: Segment the results by distribution channel and intermediary
actions: Slice the dashboard by channel: tied agents, independent intermediaries, bancassurance partners, direct digital and comparison-website introducers.

Produce an intermediary scorecard listing the twenty worst intermediaries by combined complaint rate, cooling-off cancellation rate and 13-month lapse rate, with their volumes so low-volume noise is visible.
Compare each channel against the whole-company average and mark channels running more than 1.5 times the average on any metric.
Send the scorecard to the Head of Distribution and the Producer Compliance Manager and place it in the committee pack as an annex.
checklist.done: channel segmentation and a twenty-name intermediary scorecard are produced and issued to Distribution and Producer Compliance.

checklist.step: Table the pack at the Conduct Risk Committee and record decisions
actions: Issue the quarterly pack — dashboard export, benchmark table, red-metric root causes, intermediary scorecard — to the Conduct Risk Committee at least five business days before the meeting.
Present each red metric with the Art. 17(1) question stated plainly: does the evidence show distribution acting in the customer's best interest, or does it show the distributor's interest winning.
Obtain a decision on each red metric: accept with monitoring, commission a thematic review, suspend a product or channel, or open a customer remediation.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute each decision with an owner and a due date and confirm the minutes are approved at the following meeting.
checklist.done: every red metric has a minuted committee decision with a named owner and due date.

checklist.step: Feed conduct evidence back into the product oversight and governance review
actions: Take every red or amber metric attributable to product design or target market into the product review file required by IDD Art. 25 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 Art. 7.
Re-test the target market statement against the observed buyer population, the 13-month lapse rate and the complaint root causes for that product.

Where the product is no longer consistent with its identified target market, propose a remedy: amend the target market, restrict the distribution strategy, re-price, or withdraw the product from sale.
Record the product review outcome and its date in the product approval file and inform every distributor of the change as Art. 25(1) requires.
checklist.done: each product-driven metric is reflected in a dated product review outcome and distributors are informed of any target-market or distribution-strategy change.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly metric report and open the tracked actions
actions: Publish the approved quarterly metric report to the Conduct Monitoring library and circulate it to the Head of Distribution, the Chief Risk Officer and each EU/EEA branch compliance lead.
Raise one GRC issue per red metric carrying the metric id, country, product, channel, root cause, committee decision, owner and due date.
Link each issue to the dashboard version and the committee minute so the audit trail survives staff turnover.
Set the issue closure rule to require two consecutive quarters inside tolerance before the owner may request closure.
checklist.done: the report is published and every red metric has a linked GRC issue carrying its committee decision, owner, due date and two-quarter closure rule.

checklist.step: Retain the quarterly pack and its source extracts
actions: Move the dashboard export, the Snowflake and CRM extracts, the benchmark PDFs, the intermediary scorecard and the committee minutes into the compliance evidence repository under Conduct Monitoring / IDD Art. 17(1) / <year>-Q<n>.
Apply the 5-year retention label measured from publication date and set the legal-hold flag on any quarter referenced in an open regulator inquiry.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by quarter, country, product and metric id.
Record the archive reference on the GRC issue for each red metric so the evidence can be produced without re-running any query.
checklist.done: the full quarterly pack is archived under a 5-year retention label and retrievable by quarter, country, product and metric id.

testing.step: Rebuild the metric population independently for the tested quarter
actions: Take the version-stamped Metric Library for the quarter and list every metric that should have been published, so a silently dropped metric is visible.
Re-extract policies in force, new business, lapses, cooling-off cancellations and complaint cases for the quarter directly from the warehouse using your own SQL, not the Conduct Monitoring views.
Compare your record counts to the published numerators and denominators metric by metric and record every difference in the workpaper.
Confirm all EU/EEA writing entities and branches are present — a missing country is a population failure, not a rounding difference.
testing.done: an independent population exists for every library metric and its record counts are compared line by line to the published pack.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source registers and the management accounts
actions: Reconcile the complaint case count to the complaints register maintained under the EIOPA complaints-handling guidelines and obtain the Complaints Manager's written explanation of any gap.
Reconcile policies in force and gross written premium to the quarter-end management accounts issued by Finance.
Reconcile inducement amounts to the commission run totals posted to the general ledger for the quarter.
List every unreconciled item with its value and hold the sample until each is explained or accepted in writing.
testing.done: complaints, exposure and inducement populations are reconciled to their source registers with every gap explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the metric sample
actions: Select 100% of metrics classified red or amber in the quarter.
Select 8 further metrics at random from the green population using a seeded, reproducible draw.
Within each sampled metric select 15 underlying records at random for tracing, weighted to the countries carrying the largest exposure.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all amber and red metrics plus 8 seeded green metrics, with a reproducible seed recorded.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled metric from the raw records
actions: Rebuild each sampled metric in a workbook from your own extract using the formula written in the version-stamped Metric Library, not the formula in the dashboard.
Compare your value to the published value and compute the variance as a percentage of the published figure.
Treat any variance above 2% as an exception and trace it to its cause: wrong denominator, wrong cohort window, excluded country or a changed formula applied without a library update.
Attach the workbook and the query text to the workpaper so the recomputation can be repeated.
testing.done: every sampled metric is recomputed from raw records with the variance quantified and causes identified for anything above 2%.

testing.step: Re-perform the benchmark comparison against the regulator source
actions: Open the EIOPA Consumer Trends Report and retail risk indicator annex cited in the benchmark table and locate the exact figure quoted for each sampled metric.
Open NAIC iSite+ ▸ MCAS ▸ Ratio Reports and confirm the quoted peer ratio matches the published report for the correct data year and line of business.
Confirm no comparator relies on a superseded edition; a comparator taken from a report that EIOPA or the NAIC has since replaced is an automatic exception.
Screenshot each source page with its publication date into the workpaper next to the internal metric it benchmarks.
testing.done: each sampled comparator traces to a current, captured regulator publication for the correct year and line.

testing.step: Trace sampled records from the dashboard back to source evidence
actions: For sampled complaint records open the case in the complaints tool and confirm the country, product, channel, root-cause code and upheld/not-upheld outcome match what fed the metric.
For sampled cooling-off cancellations open the policy in the policy administration system and confirm the cancellation date falls inside the 14-day withdrawal window recorded against the contract.
For sampled inducement records open the commission statement and confirm the intermediary code, amount and product agree with the metric input.
Log any record whose classification in the metric differs from its classification in the source system as a data-integrity exception.
testing.done: each sampled record traces to its source case, policy or commission statement with identifiers and classification agreeing.

testing.step: Recompute the tolerance breach maths and the publication deadline
actions: Recompute for each sampled metric whether the value breaches the amber and red tolerances recorded in the version-stamped library, and compare to the published classification.
Recompute the three-consecutive-quarters amber rule from the prior three published packs and confirm any metric caught by it was escalated to red.
Recompute the publication date as quarter-end plus 20 business days and compare it to the actual dashboard publish timestamp; count late days.
Confirm the Q4 pack was available before 1 March so it could feed the 30 April NAIC MCAS submission, and note the number of days of slack.
testing.done: tolerance classifications, the three-quarter amber rule and the 20-business-day publication deadline are all recomputed with late days counted.

testing.step: Test that every red metric produced a real, tracked response
actions: For every red metric confirm a GRC issue exists carrying root cause, country, product, channel, owner and due date, and that it pre-dates the following quarter's pack.
Confirm the Conduct Risk Committee minute records a decision for that metric and that the decision matches the issue actually raised.
Confirm any product-driven red metric appears in the Art. 25 product review file with a dated review outcome, and that distributors were informed of any target-market change.
Treat a red metric with no issue, no minute or no product review entry as a control failure rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every red metric has a matching GRC issue, a committee minute and, where product-driven, a dated Art. 25 product review entry.

testing.step: Log the exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the metric id, the quarter, what failed (recomputation variance, stale benchmark, missing escalation, data-integrity mismatch) and the conduct impact.
Assign a root cause from the standing list — formula changed without a library update, feed missing a country, benchmark not refreshed, escalation rule not applied — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarterly cycle so the fix is provable at the next test.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across sampled metrics and compare it to the two-fail ineffective threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each supporting point.
Have the independent reviewer, who computed no metric in the pack and sits outside Market Conduct Compliance, sign the workpaper and date the signature.
Report the conclusion and any open breaches to the Conduct Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Keeps the standing market-conduct exam file current — including the Art. 25 product oversight and governance evidence for every manufactured product — and is the single point of contact for an examiner or national competent authority call letter

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 25 with Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 Arts. 3-8 (manufacturer POG duties) and Art. 10 (distribution arrangements), plus IDD Art. 17 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 5, re-read against the EUR-Lex consolidated text at each annual file refresh

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the exam-ready evidence set for every product manufactured for sale to customers: product approval process, target market statement, risk assessment, product testing, distribution strategy, distributor information pack and the scheduled product review

In-scope systems.value: Standing exam file held in the compliance evidence repository with source records pulled from the product approval workflow, the policy administration system and the producer licensing system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Exam Readiness Procedure — the index of the standing file, the owner and refresh cadence of each section, and the 10-business-day drill for answering an examiner call letter or NCA information request

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Conduct Risk Committee; the file index is re-approved annually and immediately after any new product launch or NAIC Market Regulation Handbook update

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: File sections refreshed on a rolling monthly cadence; examiner call letters answered by the date stated in the letter (commonly 10-30 days); NCA information requests answered inside the deadline in the request, with an extension sought in writing before day 5 if it cannot be met

Deadline reminders configured.value: Monthly section-refresh tasks per file owner, an annual full-index review each January, and an automatic task chain the day a call letter is logged setting internal milestones at day 3 (scoping), day 7 (draft response) and day 10 (counsel clearance)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Product approval files, target market statements, product review records, distributor information packs and prior exam files retained 5 years after the product is withdrawn from sale, and 7 years for any file cited in a completed examination

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any product found without a current target market statement, product review or distributor information pack is logged as a POG exception with owner and closure date and blocks new distribution appointments for that product

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off completion of every gap closed in the standing file and personally approves the final response before it leaves for the examiner or the national competent authority

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every product manufactured and offered for sale in the EU/EEA during the year, plus every section of the standing exam file and every examiner or NCA information request received in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a product on sale without an approved target market statement, a documented risk assessment, a distribution strategy or a review inside its stated review interval is a fail; any file section more than one refresh cycle stale is a fail; one or more fails escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so file completeness is tested quarterly on a rolling product sample and in full annually, with an immediate test triggered whenever a call letter arrives

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain any section of the standing file and must not have authored the product approval documents under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual and quarterly exam-readiness test workpapers filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exam Readiness, cross-linked to each product approval file tested

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Company profile, org chart, written procedures, complaint register, licensing and appointment records, product approval and review files, IPIDs, training records and remuneration policy, producible as a complete examiner package within 10 business days of a call letter

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the examiner and NCA relationship and issues all responses; Regulatory Counsel clears anything that concedes a deficiency and manages any privileged material before it is disclosed

checklist.step: Maintain the standing exam file index and its owners
actions: Open the Exam Readiness folder in the compliance evidence repository and confirm the index carries the twelve standing sections: company and licensing profile, org chart and reporting lines, written distribution procedures, complaint register, producer licensing and appointment records, product approval and POG files, IPIDs and disclosure templates, advertising and marketing approvals, training records, remuneration and inducement policy, outsourcing and distributor agreements, and prior exam and remediation history.
Against each section record the named owner, the refresh cadence and the date the section was last refreshed.
Chase any section more than one cadence stale in writing to the named owner with a five-business-day fix date.
Re-approve the index annually with the Head of Compliance and immediately after any product launch that adds a new section.
checklist.done: the twelve-section index is current, each section has a named owner, cadence and refresh date, and nothing is more than one cadence stale.

checklist.step: Refresh the company, licensing and appointment profile
actions: In NIPR Gateway run the Producer Database report for every state and line the company writes, and export the active appointment list with effective dates.
Pull the company licence records from the NAIC UCAA corporate amendments file and confirm the writing company names, NAIC co-codes and lines of authority match the entities actually distributing.

For EU/EEA distribution export the registration records held with each national competent authority (for example the Central Bank of Ireland register or the BaFin Vermittlerregister entry) with registration numbers and passporting notifications.

Reconcile the appointment and registration lists to the intermediaries actually paid commission in the last quarter and raise any intermediary paid without a live appointment or registration as an urgent exception.
File the refreshed export in the licensing section with the run date on the file name.
checklist.done: appointment and registration exports are refreshed, reconciled to intermediaries actually paid, and any unlicensed payee is raised as an urgent exception.

checklist.step: Keep the product approval file complete for every manufactured product
actions: For each product on sale confirm the approval file holds the six Art. 25 / Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 artefacts: the written product approval process, the identified target market statement, the assessment of all relevant risks to that target market, the product testing evidence, the distribution strategy, and the scheduled review interval with its rationale.
Confirm the target market statement names both the target market and the negative target market — the customers for whom the product is not compatible — as Art. 5 of the delegated regulation expects.
Confirm product testing evidence shows scenario analysis of customer outcomes, including the effect of charges over the holding period for insurance-based investment products.
Where any artefact is missing, freeze new distributor appointments for the product and open a POG exception rather than back-filling the document with a current date.
Store each artefact in the product folder named <product>-<artefact>-<approval date>.
checklist.done: every product on sale has all six POG artefacts on file, including a negative target market, or is frozen for new appointments with an open exception.

checklist.step: Run the scheduled product review and record its outcome
actions: Check the review interval recorded in each product approval file and list every product whose review is due inside the next quarter.

Assemble the review inputs: sales volumes against the target market, 13-month lapse and cooling-off cancellation rates, complaint root causes, claims declinature rates and, for IBIPs, actual charges against the illustrated charges.

Assess whether the product remains consistent with the needs of the identified target market and whether the distribution strategy remains appropriate, and write the conclusion into the review record.
Where the review finds a mismatch, decide the remedy — amend the target market, restrict the distribution strategy, re-price, or withdraw from sale — and set the implementation date.
Notify every distributor of the review outcome and of any change to the target market or distribution strategy, and keep the distribution list as evidence.
checklist.done: each due product has a dated review record with inputs, conclusion, remedy where needed, and evidence that distributors were notified.

checklist.step: Keep the distributor information pack current and issued
actions: Assemble the pack the manufacturer must give distributors under Art. 25(1): target market statement, negative target market, distribution strategy, product features and risks, charges structure, and the information the distributor needs to identify the target market.
Publish the current pack version to the Broker & Agent Portal under Product Governance and set it as required reading for every appointed intermediary distributing the product.
Track acknowledgement per intermediary and chase non-acknowledgers at 15 and 30 days; suspend product access at 45 days.
Where a product review changes the target market, republish within 10 business days and restart the acknowledgement cycle.
checklist.done: the current pack is published per product with acknowledgement tracked per intermediary and access suspended for non-acknowledgers at 45 days.

checklist.step: Keep the complaint register exam-ready
actions: Confirm the register records for every complaint: receipt date, complainant, country, product, distribution channel, intermediary, subject matter mapped to the EIOPA complaints-handling taxonomy, acknowledgement date, resolution date, outcome and redress paid.

Confirm each complaint shows the final response was issued inside the internal service standard and that the customer was told about the relevant out-of-court redress body — the national ombudsman or FIN-NET member — as Art. 15 IDD requires.
Produce a rolling 36-month register export on the first working day of each month and file it in the exam file so no export has to be built under examiner pressure.
Flag any complaint alleging mis-selling, unsuitable advice or non-disclosure for inclusion in the exam file's high-risk case bundle.
checklist.done: a rolling 36-month register export with taxonomy coding, ombudsman signposting and a high-risk case bundle sits in the exam file, refreshed monthly.

checklist.step: Keep the disclosure and advertising evidence current
actions: Hold the live version and full version history of every Insurance Product Information Document produced under Art. 20(5) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469, with the effective date of each version.
Hold the Art. 18 and Art. 19 distributor disclosure templates covering identity, registration number, holdings, complaints routes and the nature of remuneration (fee, commission, other).
Hold the approval record for every marketing communication in market: reviewer, approval date, expiry date and the fair-clear-not-misleading assessment against Art. 17(2).
Withdraw and archive any communication whose approval has expired and record the withdrawal date.
checklist.done: current and historic IPIDs, Art. 18/19 disclosure templates and dated marketing approvals are held, with expired material archived.

checklist.step: Keep the remuneration and inducement evidence in the file
actions: Hold the remuneration policy showing how sales-force and intermediary pay is designed not to conflict with the duty to act in the customer's best interest under Art. 17(3).

Hold the per-arrangement inducement assessments required for insurance-based investment products under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Arts. 8-9, each naming the quality-enhancing benefit relied on and the evidence for it.
Hold the conflicts of interest policy and register maintained under Art. 28, with the mitigations applied to each recorded conflict.
Refresh all three annually and immediately on any change to a commission scale or a distributor agreement.
checklist.done: the remuneration policy, per-arrangement inducement assessments and the conflicts register are on file and refreshed annually and on change.

checklist.step: Keep training and competence evidence retrievable per individual
actions: Produce a per-individual training statement from the LMS for every employee and manager responsible for distribution, showing hours completed against the Art. 10(2) minimum of 15 hours per year and the Annex I knowledge areas covered.
Produce the product-specific training completion record for every product launched or materially changed in the period.
Confirm each record carries the individual's name, role, completion date, hours and the course reference so an examiner can pick a name and get a statement in minutes.
Export the statements monthly into the training section of the exam file rather than relying on live LMS access during an examination.
checklist.done: a per-individual training statement showing 15-hour attainment and Annex I coverage is exported monthly into the exam file.

checklist.step: Hold the prior examination and remediation history
actions: File every prior market conduct examination report, NCA thematic review finding and consent order with its date, the regulator and the lines examined.
Against each finding record the corrective action taken, the completion date and the evidence reference proving closure.
Flag any finding whose corrective action is still open — repeat findings are the single most damaging outcome of a follow-up examination.
Produce a one-page history summary listing regulator, year, scope, findings count and open items, refreshed each quarter.
checklist.done: every prior finding is on file with its corrective action, closure evidence and open/closed status, summarised on a refreshed one-pager.

checklist.step: Rehearse the call-letter drill twice a year
actions: Twice a year issue a simulated examiner call letter requesting five standard items: the complaint register for a named period, the underwriting and sales file for ten named policies, the producer appointment list, the product approval file for a named product, and the training statement for three named individuals.
Time the response end to end and record where the ten-business-day clock was at risk.
Record every item that could not be produced from the standing file and open a gap action against its owner.
Report the drill result to the Conduct Risk Committee with the elapsed time and the gap list.
checklist.done: a timed drill is run twice yearly with elapsed time recorded, gaps opened against owners and the result reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Log and scope any real examiner or NCA request the day it lands
actions: Log the call letter or information request in the tracker the day it arrives with regulator, examiner-in-charge, scope, examination period, lines of business and the stated response date.
Break the request into numbered items and assign each to a named owner with an internal due date three business days before the regulator deadline.
Where the deadline is not achievable, write to the examiner-in-charge before day 5 requesting an extension and stating the date you can meet — never let a deadline pass silently.
Open a single response folder so every item is assembled in one place with its source reference.
checklist.done: the request is logged with scope and deadline, split into owned numbered items with internal dates, and any extension requested in writing before day 5.

checklist.step: Assemble and quality-check the examiner package
actions: Assemble the responses into the numbered structure the examiner used, one PDF per item, each bookmarked and text-searchable.
Check every extract states its source system, run date and the parameters used, so the examiner can see it was not hand-edited.
Redact only what Regulatory Counsel has instructed and log every redaction with its basis on a redaction schedule.
Produce a transmittal index listing item number, document name, page count and source, and place it at the front of the package.
checklist.done: a bookmarked, searchable, indexed package is assembled item by item with every extract stating its source and run date and every redaction logged.

checklist.step: Clear the package through counsel and issue it
actions: Read every response item and challenge anything that concedes a deficiency, states a legal conclusion or discloses privileged advice.
Confirm the package answers what was asked and no more — volunteering unrequested material widens the examination scope.
Approve the transmittal in writing, then have the Head of Compliance sign it before it goes to the examiner-in-charge or the national competent authority.
File the issued package, the transmittal and the counsel approval in the exam file under the examination reference.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared and the Head of Compliance has signed the package, and the issued version is filed under the examination reference.

checklist.step: Retain the exam file and refresh it after the examination closes
actions: Archive the issued package, examiner correspondence, interview notes and the final report under Market Conduct / Examinations / <regulator>-<year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label to anything cited in a completed examination and the 5-years-from-withdrawal label to product approval files.
Fold every question the examiner asked that the standing file could not answer into the file index as a new or expanded section.
Confirm the archive is searchable by regulator, year, product and examination reference.
checklist.done: the examination archive is labelled for retention, searchable by regulator and product, and the standing index has absorbed every unanswerable question.

testing.step: Build the population of products and file sections that must be exam-ready
actions: Extract from the policy administration system every product with new business written in the period, by writing entity and country, so the product population comes from sales data rather than from the product catalogue.
List every section of the standing exam file index with its stated owner and refresh cadence.
Add every examiner call letter and NCA information request logged in the tracker during the period.
Confirm the extract covers all EU/EEA entities and branches and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: a signed population exists covering products actually sold, all file sections and all regulator requests in the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the product population to the product approval register
actions: Match each product sold to a product approval file on product code and writing entity.
List any product with sales but no approval file — this is the highest-severity POG finding available and needs no further analysis to report.
List any approval file with no sales and confirm the product is genuinely withdrawn rather than dormant but still open to distributors.
Obtain the Insurance Product Dev Lead's written explanation of each unmatched item before sampling.
testing.done: every product sold is matched to an approval file, with unmatched products listed and explained in writing before sampling.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of insurance-based investment products and 100% of products launched or materially changed in the period.
Select 12 further products at random from the remainder using a seeded, reproducible draw, weighted to the largest new business volumes.
Select 100% of examiner and NCA requests received in the period.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the draw can be repeated.
testing.done: the sample covers all IBIPs, all new or changed products, 12 seeded others and every regulator request, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the POG completeness assessment on each sampled product
actions: For each sampled product open the approval folder and reach your own conclusion on whether all six Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 artefacts are present before looking at the maintained checklist.
Read the target market statement and confirm it names a negative target market and describes customer needs, characteristics and objectives rather than reciting product features.
Read the risk assessment and confirm it addresses charges, complexity, liquidity and biometric risk as they land on the identified target market.
Compare your conclusion to the maintained checklist; a difference is an exception, including a product marked complete on the strength of a template with no product-specific content.
testing.done: each sampled product has an independent completeness conclusion with template-only artefacts called out as exceptions.

testing.step: Test that reviews happened inside their stated interval
actions: Read the review interval recorded in each sampled product's approval file and compute the date the review was due.
Compare the due date to the date of the most recent completed review record and count overdue days.

Confirm the review used real outcome data — sales against target market, lapse and cancellation rates, complaints and, for IBIPs, actual against illustrated charges — rather than a management assertion.
Confirm any target market or distribution strategy change arising from the review was notified to distributors and that the notification evidence exists.
testing.done: each sampled product's review is confirmed inside its interval with overdue days counted, real outcome inputs evidenced and distributor notification traced.

testing.step: Trace the distributor pack and its acknowledgement to identified intermediaries
actions: For each sampled product open the Product Governance area of the Broker & Agent Portal and confirm the published pack version matches the current approved target market statement.
Pull the acknowledgement report and pick ten intermediaries who sold the product in the period.
Confirm each of those ten acknowledged the current pack version before their first sale of that version, using acknowledgement timestamps against first-sale dates.
Log any intermediary who sold without acknowledging as an exception with the intermediary code and the sales volume involved.
testing.done: the published pack matches the approved target market and ten selling intermediaries per sampled product are traced to a pre-sale acknowledgement.

testing.step: Test file freshness and the reconciliation of licensing to payments
actions: For each standing file section compute days since last refresh against its stated cadence and count sections more than one cadence stale.
Re-run the NIPR Producer Database appointment export yourself for a sampled state and compare it to the copy held in the exam file.
Reconcile the appointment and NCA registration lists to intermediaries actually paid commission in the period and list any payee without a live appointment or registration.
Treat every unlicensed or unregistered payee as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: stale sections are counted, the licensing export is independently re-run, and any intermediary paid without a live appointment is reported as a breach.

testing.step: Recompute the response-deadline maths on every regulator request
actions: For each logged call letter or NCA request read the stated response date and the date the package was issued, and compute days early or late.
Recompute the internal milestone dates (day 3 scoping, day 7 draft, day 10 counsel clearance) and confirm each was met.
Where an extension was taken, confirm it was requested in writing before day 5 and granted in writing by the regulator.
Confirm the drill run twice in the year was completed and its gap actions closed, and count any gap still open.
testing.done: every regulator request has recomputed timeliness, evidenced extensions and confirmed drill completion with open gaps counted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the product or file section, what was missing or stale, and the exam exposure it creates.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — artefact never produced, template used without product-specific content, review interval not scheduled, pack not republished after a change, section owner vacant — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any product on sale without a complete POG file, apply the new-appointment freeze until closure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly readiness test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where a POG file is incomplete, an active distribution freeze.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across sampled products and file sections and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for products on sale without a complete POG file.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no section of the standing file and authored none of the sampled approval documents, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any distribution freezes and any unlicensed-payee breaches to the Conduct Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the remediation log for every market conduct examination finding, NCA thematic review action and internal conduct breach, and reports slippage to the Head of Compliance weekly

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17(1) and Art. 30(3) with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 16, checked against the EUR-Lex consolidated text when each finding is scoped, alongside the specific article or bulletin the examiner cited in the finding itself

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven remediation running from receipt of a draft examination report or NCA finding through rebuttal, corrective action plan, customer redress where warranted, evidence of closure and regulator confirmation, across every EU/EEA and US jurisdiction where a finding is raised

In-scope systems.value: Findings, corrective actions, owners, due dates and closure evidence tracked as issues in the GRC platform with the source examination reference on every record

Compliance procedure documented.value: Examination Findings Remediation Procedure — rebuttal window, corrective action plan template, redress calculation method, closure evidence standard and the escalation ladder when a due date is at risk

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Audit Committee; reviewed annually and after every completed examination so lessons from the last cycle are written in

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rebuttal to a draft examination report filed inside the window stated in the transmittal (commonly 30 days); corrective action plan submitted by the date in the final report or consent order; interim status reports to the regulator on the cadence the order sets, typically quarterly

Deadline reminders configured.value: On logging a finding the tracker raises reminders at rebuttal minus 10 days, plan submission minus 15 days, and at 30/14/7/1 days before every corrective action due date, with automatic escalation to the Head of Compliance on the day a due date is missed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and final reports, rebuttals, corrective action plans, redress calculations, closure evidence and regulator confirmations retained 7 years from the date the regulator confirms closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any corrective action passing its due date without an approved extension is logged as a remediation breach with root cause, revised date and Head of Compliance sign-off

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs closure of every finding against the closure evidence and approves every date extension before the original date passes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every examination finding, NCA thematic action, consent order undertaking and internal conduct breach open at any point in the period, with their corrective actions, redress populations and closure evidence

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A finding fails if it closed without evidence proving the control now works, if it closed after its due date with no approved extension, if redress was calculated on an incomplete population, or if the same root cause reappears in a later finding; any repeat finding escalates to the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven, so the test runs on every finding closed in the quarter plus all findings still open at quarter-end, with a full re-test of closed findings twelve months after closure to prove the fix held

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own any corrective action under test and must not sit in the function that raised or executed the remediation

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly remediation test workpaper filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Remediation, cross-linked to each GRC finding record tested

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Finding-by-finding closure pack — corrective action plan, evidence of the changed control, redress schedule with payment proof and the post-implementation test result — producible for any examiner follow-up within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Compliance owns the status reporting to the examiner-in-charge or NCA supervisor; Regulatory Counsel clears every rebuttal and every admission of a breach, and handles any consent order or administrative penalty negotiation

checklist.step: Log the draft report and decode every finding into a discrete obligation
actions: Log the draft examination report or NCA finding letter in the GRC platform the day it arrives with regulator, examination reference, examination period, lines examined and the transmittal date that starts the rebuttal clock.

Split the report into one issue record per finding — never one record for the whole report — each carrying the examiner's wording verbatim, the article or statute cited, the error rate found and the population the examiner tested.
Classify each finding as criticism, violation, or recommendation, because the rebuttal strategy and the redress obligation differ across the three.
Assign a provisional owner from the function that runs the failed control and copy the Head of Compliance on the full list within two business days.
checklist.done: each finding is a separate tracked issue carrying verbatim wording, the cited authority, the examiner's error rate and a provisional owner.

checklist.step: Verify the factual basis of each finding before conceding it
actions: Request the examiner's underlying sample list — policy numbers, claim numbers or complaint references — through the examiner-in-charge and reconcile it to your own systems.
Re-perform the examiner's test on the same records and compute your own error count and error rate.
Separate genuine control failures from data-extract artefacts, misread system fields and records outside the examination period, and document which is which record by record.
Where you disagree, assemble the source evidence — screenshots, dated procedure versions, system audit trails — that shows the record was handled correctly.
Hand the analysis to Regulatory Counsel with a recommended position of concede, partially concede, or rebut for each finding.
checklist.done: the examiner's sample is reconciled and re-performed record by record, with a documented concede/rebut recommendation per finding.

checklist.step: File the rebuttal inside the response window
actions: Read the transmittal letter for the exact rebuttal deadline — commonly 30 days from the draft report date — and diary it with a 10-day warning.
Draft the response finding by finding, stating for each: accepted, accepted in part, or disputed, with the evidence reference supporting the position.
Keep the tone factual and avoid volunteering issues the examiner did not raise, while never disputing a finding you cannot evidence.
Obtain the Head of Compliance signature and submit through the channel the examiner specified, retaining the submission confirmation.
Where the deadline cannot be met, request an extension in writing before the halfway point and record the regulator's written reply.
checklist.done: a signed, evidence-referenced rebuttal is submitted inside the stated window with the submission confirmation retained.

checklist.step: Write a corrective action plan against every accepted finding
actions: For each accepted finding write the plan on the standard template: root cause, the control change that fixes it, the owner, the completion date and the evidence that will prove closure.
Distinguish the immediate containment step (stop the harm now) from the sustainable fix (change the process, system or training) and date both separately.
Set completion dates that respect the regulator's stated deadline in the final report or consent order, and never propose a date you cannot resource.
Have each named owner accept their action in writing in the tracker before the plan is submitted.
Submit the plan to the examiner-in-charge or NCA supervisor by the date stated in the final report and file the acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every accepted finding has an owner-accepted plan with containment and sustainable fix dated separately, submitted by the regulator's deadline.

checklist.step: Establish the root cause rather than the symptom
actions: Run a structured root cause analysis on each finding with the process owner, taking the failure back at least three levels from the symptom.
Classify the root cause: procedure absent or wrong, system control missing, training gap, incentive conflict under Art. 17(3), third-party distributor failure, or data quality.
Test whether the same root cause affects other products, countries or channels beyond the examined scope and record the extended exposure.
Where the extended exposure is material, widen the corrective action to cover it rather than fixing only the examined jurisdiction.
checklist.done: each finding has a three-level root cause analysis, a classified cause and a documented assessment of exposure beyond the examined scope.

checklist.step: Size the affected customer population where harm is possible
actions: Build the full population of customers potentially affected by the failed control over the whole period the failure existed, not just the examination period.
Define the population rule in writing (product, country, channel, date range, control field values) and have the Compliance Manager approve it before extraction.
Reconcile the population count to policies in force and new business for the same period so an under-scoped extract is visible.
Segment the population into harmed, potentially harmed and unaffected using the criteria in the corrective action plan and hand the file to Consumer Affairs.
checklist.done: an approved, reconciled population covering the full failure period is segmented into harmed, potentially harmed and unaffected.

checklist.step: Calculate and pay customer redress where the finding warrants it
actions: Apply the approved redress method per customer: premium or charge refund, restoration of the position the customer would have been in, plus interest at the rate the regulator or the national ombudsman expects.
Produce a redress schedule listing policy number, customer, harm identified, amount, interest, calculation date and payment reference.
Issue the customer communication explaining what went wrong, what is being paid and the right to refer the matter to the national out-of-court redress body, and retain a copy per customer.
Instruct payment through the policy administration and payment systems and reconcile paid amounts back to the schedule, chasing unpaid items at 30 days.
Track goneaway and returned payments separately with the tracing steps taken.
checklist.done: a per-customer redress schedule is calculated, communicated, paid and reconciled, with goneaways tracked and unpaid items chased at 30 days.

checklist.step: Change the procedure and the system control that failed
actions: Rewrite the affected written procedure with the corrected step, version it, date it and route it for approval by the accountable function head.

Specify the system change that makes the failure hard to repeat — a mandatory field, a hard block, a validation rule, a workflow gate — and raise it with the owning platform team with the finding reference attached.
Have the change tested in a non-production environment against the exact scenario the examiner found and keep the test evidence.
Record the production release date and confirm the control is live in every country and entity in scope, not just the examined one.
checklist.done: the procedure is reissued and the system control is released, tested against the examiner's scenario and confirmed live across all in-scope entities.

checklist.step: Retrain the people whose behaviour the finding exposed
actions: Build a targeted module covering the failed behaviour, the corrected procedure and the customer harm it caused, and map it to the Annex I knowledge areas so the hours count toward the Art. 10(2) 15-hour requirement.
Assign it in the LMS to the exact population identified by the root cause analysis — the named individuals, team or intermediary panel — with a completion deadline inside the corrective action date.
Track completion weekly, escalate non-completers to their manager at 14 days and suspend new business authority at 30 days.
Export the completion record into the finding's closure evidence folder.
checklist.done: a targeted module is assigned to the identified population with completion tracked, non-completers escalated and the record exported as closure evidence.

checklist.step: Manage due dates and escalate slippage before it becomes a breach
actions: Run the open-actions report every Monday filtered to due within 30 days and overdue, and review it with each action owner.
Where an owner forecasts slippage, require a written extension request before the original date stating the new date, the reason and the interim control holding the risk.
Escalate any request to move a date agreed with a regulator to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel, since it usually requires notifying the examiner.
Log any action that passes its date without an approved extension as a remediation breach with root cause and a Head of Compliance sign-off.
checklist.done: a weekly open-actions review runs, extensions are approved in writing before the original date, and every missed date is logged as a breach.

checklist.step: Prove closure with evidence that the control now works
actions: For each completed action assemble the closure evidence: the reissued procedure with version and date, the release note for the system control, the training completion export, and the redress reconciliation.
Run a post-implementation sample of at least 25 transactions processed after the fix date and confirm zero recurrences of the examined failure.
Where a recurrence appears, refuse closure and reopen the action rather than closing on the strength of the fix being deployed.
Attach the sample results to the finding record with the transaction identifiers tested.
checklist.done: each action carries closure evidence plus a post-implementation sample of 25 or more transactions showing zero recurrence.

checklist.step: Report status to the regulator on the cadence the order requires
actions: Read the final report or consent order for the reporting cadence and format and diary each status report date.
Draft the status report finding by finding: action, status, completion date, evidence available, and redress paid to date with customer and value counts.
State slipped dates plainly with the revised date and the reason — a regulator finding a concealed slip treats it far more seriously than the slip itself.
Have the Head of Compliance sign each report before submission and retain the regulator's acknowledgement.
checklist.done: each required status report is submitted on time, signed, and states slipped dates openly with revised dates and reasons.

checklist.step: Obtain sign-off and formal closure for each finding
actions: Review the closure pack for each finding and challenge any closure resting on deployment alone rather than on evidence the control now works.
Sign and date the closure on the finding record, naming the evidence relied on.
Where the regulator must confirm closure, submit the closure pack and record the regulator's written confirmation against the finding.
Report closed and open findings to the Audit Committee each quarter with ageing and any repeat findings named.
checklist.done: each finding carries a dated closure signature naming its evidence, plus regulator confirmation where required, and is reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Re-test twelve months after closure to prove the fix held
actions: Diary a twelve-month post-closure re-test on every finding at the moment it closes.
Re-run the examiner's original test on a fresh sample of at least 25 transactions from the twelve months after closure.

Where the failure has returned, reopen the finding as a repeat, notify Regulatory Counsel the same day, and treat the recurrence as an Art. 17(1) governance failure rather than a fresh operational error.
File the re-test result against the original finding record so a follow-up examination can see the sustained fix.
checklist.done: every closed finding has a diarised twelve-month re-test whose result is filed against the original record, with recurrences reopened as repeats.

checklist.step: Retain the remediation file for the full period
actions: Archive the draft and final reports, rebuttal, corrective action plan, root cause analysis, redress schedule and payment proofs, training exports and closure evidence under Market Conduct / Remediation / <regulator>-<year>-<finding id>.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the regulator's closure confirmation and set legal hold where an order or penalty remains live.
Confirm the archive is searchable by regulator, finding id, product, country and root cause so repeat causes can be found across cycles.
Record the archive reference on the GRC finding record.
checklist.done: the remediation file is archived under a 7-year label, searchable by finding id and root cause, and referenced from the GRC record.

testing.step: Build the population of findings and corrective actions for the period
actions: Extract from the GRC platform every finding open at any point in the period with regulator, examination reference, date raised, due date, status and owner.
Add findings raised outside the tracker by checking regulator correspondence logs and Audit Committee minutes, so a finding managed by email is visible.
Confirm each examination report in the period has as many tracked findings as the report itself lists, page by page.
Sign the population as complete once the report-to-tracker count agrees.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled page by page to the underlying examination reports and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the corrective actions to the plans submitted to the regulator
actions: Obtain the corrective action plans as actually submitted to the examiner or NCA and compare them line by line to the actions in the tracker.
List any action promised to the regulator that has no tracker record and any tracker action whose due date differs from the date promised.
Confirm every date change was covered by a written extension approved before the original date and, where the date was regulator-agreed, notified to the regulator.
Hold the sample until every difference is explained in writing by the Compliance Manager.
testing.done: tracker actions reconcile line by line to the submitted plans, with every date difference explained and every extension evidenced.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of findings classified as violations and 100% of findings carrying customer redress.
Select 100% of findings closed in the period, since closure quality is the point of the test.
Select 10 further open findings at random from the remainder using a seeded, reproducible draw.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all violations, all redress findings, all closures and 10 seeded open findings, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the examiner's test on each sampled closed finding
actions: Read the examiner's original test method and error definition from the report rather than from the tracker summary.
Draw 25 transactions processed after the recorded fix date from the policy administration system for the same product, country and channel.
Apply the examiner's error definition yourself and compute your own error rate before reading the company's post-implementation sample.
Any recurrence is an exception and, where the finding is already closed, a reportable repeat rather than a documentation point.
testing.done: each closed finding has an independent 25-transaction re-performance with an auditor-computed error rate and recurrences flagged as repeats.

testing.step: Test the completeness of the redress population
actions: Read the approved population rule and rebuild the affected-customer population yourself over the full period the control failed.
Compare your count to the redress schedule count and investigate any shortfall — a population truncated to the examination period is the most common defect here.
Trace 15 customers from your population into the redress schedule and confirm each received a calculation, a communication and a payment.
Trace 15 payments from the schedule back to the payment system and confirm value, date and payee agree.
testing.done: the redress population is independently rebuilt over the full failure period and traced both ways on 15 records each side.

testing.step: Recompute redress amounts and interest on a sample
actions: Recompute the redress for 15 sampled customers using the approved method — refund or restoration of position — from the underlying premium, charge and transaction data.
Recompute the interest from the date of harm to the date of payment at the rate the regulator or ombudsman expects and compare to the amount paid.
Quantify any underpayment in total across the population by extrapolating the sampled error rate and report the figure, not just the sampled variance.
Attach the recomputation workbook and the source data extract to the workpaper.
testing.done: redress and interest are recomputed on 15 customers with any underpayment extrapolated across the population and quantified.

testing.step: Trace the control change to evidence it is live everywhere in scope
actions: For each sampled finding open the reissued procedure and confirm its version, approval signature and effective date pre-date the claimed closure.
Open the system release note and confirm the control shipped, then observe the control operating in the live environment on a real transaction.
Confirm the control is live in every country and legal entity named in the extended-exposure assessment, not only the examined jurisdiction.
Log a partial deployment as an exception even where the examined jurisdiction is fixed.
testing.done: each control change is traced to a dated procedure, a release note and an observed live control across every in-scope entity.

testing.step: Recompute deadline and ageing arithmetic across the portfolio
actions: Recompute for each sampled finding the days between raised date and due date, and between due date and actual closure, and count overdue days.
Recompute the rebuttal deadline from the draft report transmittal date and compare to the submission date on the retained confirmation.
Recompute the status-report dates required by the order and compare to submission dates, counting late reports.
Compute portfolio ageing — findings open over 90, 180 and 365 days — and compare to what was reported to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: rebuttal, closure and status-report timeliness are recomputed and portfolio ageing is compared to what the Audit Committee was told.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the finding id, the regulator, what failed in the remediation and the regulatory exposure it creates.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — closed on deployment not evidence, redress population truncated, extension taken after the date, partial deployment, repeat cause not extended beyond the examined jurisdiction — and name an owner.
For any repeat finding, notify Regulatory Counsel the same day and assess whether the regulator must be told before the next scheduled status report.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with repeats notified to counsel the same day.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over sampled findings and compare it to the fail criteria, treating any repeat finding as automatically escalating.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each point.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no corrective action and sits outside the remediating function, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, repeat findings and any extrapolated redress shortfall to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
