checklist.step: Define the mandatory question set for each product family
actions: Write the question set per product family so each Art. 20(1) element is captured explicitly: what the customer wants covered, the risk they are protecting against, existing cover already held, budget, and any circumstance that would make the product unsuitable.

For insurance-based investment products add the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9 elements: knowledge and experience in the relevant product type, financial situation including the ability to bear losses, and investment objectives including risk tolerance and holding period.

Add the sustainability preference questions required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1257 — whether the customer wants a minimum proportion of sustainable investment or principal adverse impact consideration, and to what degree.
Map each question to the target market statement of every product in the family so the answers can be tested against the target market at recommendation time.
Obtain Head of Compliance and Head of Distribution approval and record the approved version and effective date.
checklist.done: an approved, version-dated question set exists per product family covering Art. 20(1), the Art. 9 IBIP elements and sustainability preferences, mapped to target markets.

checklist.step: Build the question set into the CRM as a gated form
actions: Configure the profile object on the CRM opportunity so each approved question is a discrete field with the correct data type, not a free-text notes box.
Make every Art. 20(1) field mandatory before the quote action can fire, and every Art. 9 IBIP field mandatory before an IBIP illustration can be produced.
Set the profile completion timestamp to be system-generated and non-editable so the sequence against inception can be proved later.
Add validation preventing an IBIP recommendation where risk tolerance conflicts with the product risk indicator, requiring a supervisor override with a written reason.
Release to a test environment, run the ten scripted scenarios provided by Compliance and keep the test evidence with the release note.
checklist.done: the profile form is live as discrete mandatory fields with a system timestamp, quote and illustration gates, and scripted scenario test evidence on file.

checklist.step: Capture the customer's demands and needs at the start of the conversation
actions: Open the CRM opportunity and start the profile before any product is named — asking demands and needs after showing a product turns the record into a justification exercise.
Record in the customer's own terms what they want to protect, the amounts and durations involved, and any events they specifically want covered or excluded.
Record existing cover already held, including cover through an employer, a mortgage or a card, so duplicate cover is visible.
Record any circumstance that would exclude the customer from a product's target market — age, occupation, residency, pre-existing condition, non-EEA travel — in the dedicated fields.
Save and let the system timestamp the profile before moving to product selection.
checklist.done: the profile is captured and system-timestamped before any product is named, with demands, existing cover and target-market exclusions in dedicated fields.

checklist.step: Complete the fuller suitability profile for insurance-based investment products
actions: Record knowledge and experience by product type, number of years and transaction frequency, not as a single self-declared 'experienced' tick.
Record the financial situation: regular income, committed outgoings, liquid assets, existing investments and the specific ability to bear losses on the amount being invested.
Record objectives: purpose, target holding period, risk tolerance on the stated scale, and whether the customer needs access to the money before the recommended term.
Record sustainability preferences as an explicit yes/no plus, where yes, the minimum proportion and the adverse-impact factors the customer cares about.
Where the customer declines to answer, record the declined field explicitly and stop — an IBIP recommendation cannot be made on an incomplete Art. 9 profile.
checklist.done: the IBIP profile carries knowledge and experience, financial situation with loss-bearing ability, objectives and explicit sustainability preferences, with declines recorded and recommendations stopped.

checklist.step: Handle telephone and digital journeys without dropping the profile
actions: Confirm the telephone script in Genesys puts the demands-and-needs questions before the product presentation and that the agent screen writes straight into the CRM profile fields.
Confirm calls where a sale is attempted are recorded and retained, and that the recording reference is written onto the CRM opportunity so the profile conversation can be replayed.
For the digital self-service journey confirm the customer cannot reach payment without completing the same mandatory fields, and that the answers land in the same CRM object as adviser-captured ones.
Review five recorded calls per agent per month against the script and coach any agent who presents a product before capturing demands and needs.
checklist.done: telephone and digital journeys write into the same gated profile fields, call recording references are on the opportunity, and five calls per agent per month are reviewed.

checklist.step: Verify the customer information rather than accepting it blind
actions: Cross-check the stated existing cover against the customer's other policies held with the company before issue.
Cross-check declared age, residency and occupation against the application data and query any mismatch with the adviser before the case proceeds.
Where the profile says the customer wants access to funds inside the recommended term of an IBIP, refer the case to the Suitability Desk rather than issuing.
Record every query raised and its answer on the case so the challenge is visible on the file.
checklist.done: profile answers are cross-checked against internal policy and application data, with every query and answer recorded on the case.

checklist.step: Produce the demands-and-needs statement and put it to the customer
actions: Generate the demands-and-needs statement from the captured fields so it restates the customer's own answers rather than a generic paragraph.
State plainly which needs the proposed contract meets and which it does not, including any need the customer raised that this product leaves uncovered.
Give the statement to the customer on a durable medium before the contract concludes, as Art. 23 requires, defaulting to paper unless the customer has chosen another durable medium.
Record the delivery date, channel and the customer's confirmation of receipt on the opportunity.
checklist.done: a customer-specific demands-and-needs statement is delivered on a durable medium before conclusion, with delivery date and confirmation recorded.

checklist.step: Issue a personalised recommendation with reasons where advice is given
actions: Where advice is given, state which product is recommended and explain, by reference to the customer's recorded answers, why it best meets their demands and needs, as Art. 20(1) third subparagraph requires.
Name the alternatives considered and why each was rejected — a recommendation with no rejected alternative reads as a product push.

For IBIPs issue the suitability report required by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 14 before the contract concludes, setting out the advice given and how it matches the customer's preferences, objectives and other characteristics.
Where the sale is non-advised, record that no advice was given and confirm the customer was told so before conclusion.
checklist.done: advised sales carry a reasoned personalised recommendation with rejected alternatives and, for IBIPs, a pre-conclusion suitability report; non-advised sales are labelled as such.

checklist.step: Handle customers who decline to provide information
actions: Record the specific fields the customer declined and the adviser's explanation of the consequence given to the customer.
For an IBIP with advice, stop the sale — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9(5) does not permit a suitability assessment on an incomplete picture.
For non-IBIP products, allow the sale only where the remaining information still supports a demands-and-needs statement, and record on the file which need could not be assessed.
Escalate any adviser with repeated declined-field sales to the Producer Compliance Manager, since a pattern usually means the questions are not being asked.
checklist.done: declined fields are recorded per file, IBIP advised sales are stopped on incomplete Art. 9 profiles, and repeat patterns are escalated.

checklist.step: Hard-gate policy issue on a complete, pre-dated profile
actions: Configure the issue step to require the CRM profile identifier and to reject issue where the identifier is absent.
Reject issue where the profile completion timestamp is later than the proposed inception date, so a back-filled profile cannot rescue a sale.
Route every rejected case to the adviser and their supervisor with the reason code and hold the case rather than allowing a manual override at operator level.
Report the rejected-case volume weekly to the Distribution Operations Manager by channel and adviser.
checklist.done: policy issue rejects any case without a profile identifier or with a profile timestamped after inception, and rejections are reported weekly by adviser.

checklist.step: Supervise profile quality in the first line
actions: Run the CRM report Distribution ▸ Profile Quality weekly showing completion rate, average fields populated, declined-field rate and free-text-only answers per adviser.

Review five files per adviser per month against the quality standard: answers specific to the customer, existing cover recorded, target-market exclusions addressed, statement delivered before conclusion.
Coach any adviser whose files repeat generic answers and record the coaching on the adviser's supervision record.
Refer any adviser failing two consecutive monthly reviews to the Producer Compliance Manager for formal action.
checklist.done: weekly quality reporting plus five files per adviser per month are reviewed, coaching is recorded and two consecutive failures are referred for formal action.

checklist.step: Remediate any contract concluded without a complete profile
actions: Take the weekly list of policies issued with a missing or late profile and open a case per policy.
Contact the customer, complete the demands-and-needs assessment properly, and test whether the contract they hold actually meets it.

Where it does, document the outcome and keep the contract in force with the completed profile attached; where it does not, offer cancellation from inception with a full premium refund and any consequential loss.
Record the outcome per customer and sign the case closed.
checklist.done: every missing-profile policy has a customer contact, a completed assessment and either a documented fit or a cancellation with full refund, signed closed.

checklist.step: Keep the question set aligned to product and rule changes
actions: On any change to a product's target market statement, review whether the question set still captures the information needed to test target-market fit and raise a change request where it does not.
On any change to the sustainability preference rules or the PRIIPs risk indicator methodology, review the affected questions with the Sustainability Risk Manager.
Route every change through the same approval as the original question set and record the new version and effective date.
Communicate changes to all channels with an effective date at least 10 business days ahead so training and system release can land first.
checklist.done: the question set is reviewed on every target-market or rule change, re-approved with a version and effective date, and communicated 10 business days ahead.

checklist.step: Train advisers on capturing rather than justifying
actions: Deliver the demands-and-needs module covering the Art. 20(1) elements, the Art. 9 IBIP additions and the sustainability preference questions, with worked good and bad file examples.
Assess competence with a practical file-build exercise rather than a multiple-choice test, and record the pass in the LMS with hours mapped to the Art. 10(2) 15-hour requirement.
Require completion before an adviser is granted CRM quote authority for a new product family.
Re-run the module for any adviser referred after two failed monthly supervision reviews.
checklist.done: advisers pass a practical file-build assessment recorded in the LMS before receiving quote authority, with re-training triggered by supervision failures.

checklist.step: Retain the per-policy profile evidence
actions: Archive the profile form, demands-and-needs statement, suitability report where applicable, adviser notes and call recording reference against the policy number in the document repository.
Apply the life-of-contract plus 5 years retention label and extend it automatically where a complaint or ombudsman case references the policy.
Confirm retrieval by policy number returns the complete pack in under 2 business days by testing five random policies each quarter.
Record the retrieval test result in the Distribution evidence folder.
checklist.done: per-policy packs are archived under a life-plus-5-years label with a quarterly five-policy retrieval test evidencing 2-business-day production.

testing.step: Build the population of policies incepted in the quarter
actions: Extract every EU/EEA policy incepted in the quarter from the policy administration system with policy number, product, country, channel, intermediary code, adviser, inception date and advised/non-advised flag.
Add digital self-service and telephone sales explicitly so a channel that bypasses adviser records cannot hide.
Reconcile the policy count and premium to the new business figures in the quarter-end management accounts and explain any difference.
Sign the population as complete before drawing the sample.
testing.done: an all-channel policy population is extracted, reconciled to management accounts new business and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to CRM profile records
actions: Match every policy to a CRM profile record on the profile identifier stored on the policy.
List every policy with no matching profile — this is an automatic fail requiring no judgement.
Compare each profile completion timestamp to the policy inception date and list every profile timestamped on or after inception as a late profile.
Obtain the Distribution Operations Manager's written explanation of each unmatched and late record before sampling.
testing.done: every policy is matched to a profile with completion timestamps compared to inception and all missing or late profiles listed as automatic fails.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of insurance-based investment product sales with advice, and 100% of sales by advisers in their first three months.
Select 40 further policies at random using a seeded, reproducible draw, stratified so every country and channel is represented.
Add 10 policies from the advisers with the highest declined-field rates identified in supervision reporting.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all advised IBIPs and new advisers plus 40 stratified and 10 risk-targeted files, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the demands-and-needs assessment on each sampled file
actions: Read the captured profile without reading the recommendation first and form your own view of what the customer needed.

Score each file on the standard attributes: answers specific to the customer, existing cover recorded, target-market exclusions addressed, budget captured, and no answer consisting only of a product name.
Compare your view to the contract actually sold and mark a mismatch where the contract does not meet a recorded need or covers a need the customer did not express.
Treat a profile of generic template answers as a fail even where every field is populated.
testing.done: each sampled file has an independent needs assessment scored on the standard attributes with template-only profiles failed.

testing.step: Test the IBIP suitability elements against the delegated regulation
actions: For each sampled IBIP file confirm all Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9 elements are present: knowledge and experience, financial situation with ability to bear losses, and objectives with risk tolerance and holding period.
Confirm the sustainability preference question was asked and answered, and that the product's SFDR classification matches a stated preference for sustainable investment.
Confirm the recommended product's risk indicator is consistent with the recorded risk tolerance, and that any override carries a documented supervisor reason.
Confirm the Art. 14 suitability report was issued and reached the customer before conclusion, or immediately after where a telephone distance sale was concluded with the customer's agreement.
testing.done: every sampled IBIP file evidences all Art. 9 elements, a sustainability match, a consistent risk indicator and a pre-conclusion suitability report.

testing.step: Trace the statement and recommendation to delivery evidence
actions: Open the archived pack for each sampled policy and confirm the demands-and-needs statement, the recommendation and any suitability report are present as issued to the customer.
Confirm the delivery record shows a durable medium and a delivery date earlier than the inception date.
Where the sale was by telephone, retrieve the call recording using the reference on the opportunity and confirm the demands-and-needs questions were asked before the product was named.
Log any file where the statement exists but no delivery evidence does as an exception — production is not delivery.
testing.done: each sampled file traces to an archived statement and recommendation with dated durable-medium delivery before inception, and telephone sales are verified on the recording.

testing.step: Test the system gate by attempting to defeat it
actions: In the test environment attempt to issue a policy with an empty profile identifier and confirm the issue step rejects it.
Attempt to issue with a profile timestamped after the proposed inception date and confirm the rejection fires.
Attempt an IBIP illustration with an incomplete Art. 9 profile and confirm the illustration is blocked.
Review the production override log for the quarter and confirm every override carries a supervisor identity and a written reason; overrides without a reason are exceptions.
testing.done: all three system gates are proven by attempted circumvention in test and every production override is evidenced with a supervisor and a reason.

testing.step: Recompute rates, thresholds and remediation timeliness
actions: Recompute the completeness error rate as failed files divided by files reviewed, overall and per adviser, and compare to the 2% overall and 10% per-adviser thresholds.
Recompute the missing-profile rate over the whole population, not the sample, since absence is measurable at population level.
For each missing-profile policy recompute the days between inception and the remediation customer contact and count any exceeding the procedure's response standard.
Extrapolate the sampled error rate over the population and state the estimated number of customers affected.
testing.done: error rates are recomputed against the 2% and 10% thresholds, the population missing-profile rate is measured and remediation timeliness is counted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per failed file recording policy number, adviser, intermediary code, channel, the attribute that failed and the customer impact.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — profile captured after product selection, template answers, declined fields not challenged, gate overridden, digital journey field not mandatory — and name an owner.
Refer any adviser with an error rate above 10% to the Producer Compliance Manager for supervision action and record the referral on the issue.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly file review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every failed file carries an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and, above 10%, an adviser referral for supervision action.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the recomputed error rates to the zero-tolerance absence rule and the 2% completeness threshold and state whether either was breached.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the per-file scoring sheets behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution, carries no sales target and supervised none of the sampled advisers, sign and date the workpaper.
Report results, extrapolated customer impact and adviser referrals to the Conduct Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, error rates against thresholds and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Register every inducement arrangement in force
actions: Read every distributor, platform and partner agreement in the contracts repository and extract each arrangement under which a fee, commission or non-monetary benefit is paid to or received from a third party in connection with IBIP distribution.

Register each arrangement with counterparty, country, products covered, benefit type (initial commission, trail, marketing allowance, training funding, technology provision, hospitality), the basis of calculation and the annual value.
Include non-monetary benefits explicitly — conference funding, systems provided free, seconded staff — because these are the ones habitually left off registers.
Reconcile the register to commission and expense postings for the year so an unregistered arrangement shows up as an unexplained payment.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the register annually and record the approval date.
checklist.done: every monetary and non-monetary IBIP inducement arrangement is registered with counterparty, basis and value, reconciled to actual payments and approved annually.

checklist.step: Run the Art. 8(2) quality-enhancement test on each arrangement
actions: For each arrangement state the additional or higher-level service the inducement funds, using the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 8(2) framing rather than a general assertion of value.
Evidence the benefit with something measurable: the advice capacity funded, the ongoing service actually delivered, the range of products made accessible, or the tooling put in front of customers.
Confirm the benefit is proportionate to the amount paid by comparing the annual inducement value to the cost of delivering the claimed service.
Confirm the arrangement does not benefit only the distributor or the manufacturer with no customer-facing improvement, and write the conclusion in plain terms.
Where the test fails, propose a redesign of the arrangement rather than a stronger write-up.
checklist.done: each arrangement carries a written quality-enhancement conclusion with measurable evidence and a proportionality comparison, or a redesign proposal.

checklist.step: Assess every Art. 8(4) detriment factor for the arrangement
actions: Work through the Art. 8(4) factors one by one for the arrangement: its nature, its value, the structure and timing of payment, whether it creates an incentive to offer or recommend a particular product, whether it relates to distribution activity, whether the benefit reaches the customer, and the relationship between the parties.
Record for each factor whether it points toward detriment and why, with the evidence relied on.
Pay particular attention to front-loaded initial commission on long-term IBIPs and to volume-triggered bonuses, since both create the clearest incentive to churn.
Reach an overall conclusion of no detrimental impact, detrimental impact mitigated, or detrimental impact — and where it is the third, stop the arrangement.
Have the conclusion challenged by a second Compliance Manager before it is filed.
checklist.done: every Art. 8(4) factor is individually assessed with evidence, an overall detriment conclusion is reached and challenged by a second reviewer.

checklist.step: Wire the assessment outcome into commission configuration
actions: Set up each approved arrangement in the commission platform with its assessment reference and the assessment expiry date on the scheme record.
Configure the platform to suspend payment under any scheme whose assessment has expired, rather than paying and reconciling later.
Where an arrangement was redesigned, retire the old scheme with an end date and confirm no payments run against it after that date.
Report weekly to the Compliance Manager any payment attempted against a suspended or retired scheme.
checklist.done: every commission scheme carries an assessment reference and expiry, payments suspend on expiry, and attempts against retired schemes are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Disclose the nature of remuneration to the customer
actions: Before the contract concludes tell the customer the nature of the remuneration received in relation to the contract — fee, commission, other, or a combination — as Art. 19(1) requires.
For IBIPs disclose all costs and charges aggregated so the customer can see the cumulative effect on the return, as Art. 29(1) requires, including third-party payment amounts where applicable.
Deliver on a durable medium before conclusion and record the delivery date on the opportunity.
Where the customer asks the amount rather than the nature, give the figure — refusing turns a compliant disclosure into a complaint.
checklist.done: the nature of remuneration and the aggregated IBIP costs and charges are disclosed on a durable medium before conclusion with the delivery date recorded.

checklist.step: Queue every advised IBIP recommendation for pre-issue review
actions: Configure the case flow so any opportunity flagged advised and IBIP moves to the Suitability Desk queue automatically after the recommendation is produced and before issue.
Attach to the queue item the profile record, the recommendation, the suitability report draft, the illustration and the product PRIIPs key information document.
Reject into the queue any case missing an attachment rather than letting the reviewer chase it.
Report queue volume and ageing to the Suitability Desk lead each morning.
checklist.done: every advised IBIP case reaches the review queue automatically with a complete attachment set, and queue ageing is reported daily.

checklist.step: Review the recommendation against the recorded customer profile
actions: Read the profile before the recommendation and form your own view of what the customer needs, so the review is not a confirmation exercise.

Test each Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 9 element against the recommendation: does the product match the recorded knowledge and experience, the ability to bear losses, the objectives, the holding period and the risk tolerance.
Test the sustainability preference against the product's SFDR classification and reject any recommendation that overrides a stated preference without the customer having adapted it in writing.
Test the recommendation against the product's target market statement and reject any sale into the negative target market.
Record the decision — approve, refer for rework, reject — with reasons tied to specific profile fields.
checklist.done: each recommendation carries an independent decision tested against every Art. 9 element, the sustainability preference and the target market, with field-level reasons.

checklist.step: Challenge the switch or replacement rationale
actions: Where the recommendation replaces an existing contract, require the file to show the existing contract's charges, surrender penalty, guarantees being given up and remaining term.
Compute the cost of switching — exit penalty plus new initial charges — and compare it to the claimed benefit over the recommended holding period.
Reject any switch whose written rationale does not survive that comparison, regardless of the customer's stated agreement.
Flag any adviser with more than three switch recommendations in a quarter to the Producer Compliance Manager for pattern review.
checklist.done: every replacement recommendation shows the existing contract's terms, a computed switching cost against benefit, and rejection where the maths fails.

checklist.step: Test the recommendation against the inducement in play
actions: For each reviewed recommendation look up the commission payable on the recommended product and on the closest rejected alternative.
Where the recommended product pays materially more and the file's reasons for rejecting the alternative are thin, refer the case for a second reviewer rather than approving it.
Record the commission differential on the review record so a pattern across an adviser or a product becomes visible in reporting.
Report monthly to the Conduct Risk Committee the share of approved recommendations that sat on the higher-paying option, by adviser and product.
checklist.done: each review records the commission differential against the rejected alternative, thin rationales are second-reviewed, and the higher-paying share is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Return rejected and reworked cases to the adviser with specifics
actions: Return the case with the specific profile field, target-market clause or Art. 9 element that failed, not a generic 'insufficient rationale'.
Set a rework deadline of two business days and hold the case out of issue until the queue item closes.
Where the same adviser is returned three times in a quarter for the same reason, escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager and to the adviser's Distribution Operations Manager.
Keep the full rejection and rework trail on the opportunity so the file shows what was challenged and what changed.
checklist.done: returns state the specific failed element, carry a two-business-day rework deadline, and the full challenge trail stays on the opportunity.

checklist.step: Block issue until the review closes
actions: Configure the issue step to require a closed Suitability Desk review reference on every advised IBIP case and reject issue where it is absent or in rework status.
Deny operator-level override; route any override request to the Suitability Desk lead with a written reason recorded on the case.
Report daily to the Head of Compliance any advised IBIP that reached issue without a closed review.
Where a case slipped through, quarantine the policy and open a customer remediation case the same day.
checklist.done: issue rejects advised IBIPs without a closed review, overrides are lead-level with written reasons, and slipped cases are quarantined and remediated the same day.

checklist.step: Re-assess arrangements annually and on any change
actions: Re-run the Art. 8(2) and Art. 8(4) assessment for every arrangement 30 days before its anniversary, using the last twelve months of actual payments and actual service delivery rather than the original projection.
Trigger an immediate re-assessment within 20 business days of any change to commission rates, scheme structure or distributor agreement terms.
Where the evidence of the claimed higher-level service has not materialised, withdraw the arrangement rather than rolling the assessment forward.
Record each re-assessment with its date, evidence and conclusion against the arrangement record.
checklist.done: each arrangement is re-assessed on actual twelve-month payment and service data before its anniversary, and within 20 business days of any change.

checklist.step: Report review outcomes and inducement conclusions upward
actions: Report to the Conduct Risk Committee each quarter: reviews performed, approval and rejection rates by adviser and product, the top rejection reasons and the higher-paying-option share.
Report the inducement register status: arrangements assessed, arrangements with detriment concerns, arrangements withdrawn or redesigned.
Escalate to the Board risk committee any arrangement continued despite an unresolved detriment concern, with the reasoning in writing.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute the decisions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: quarterly review statistics and inducement register status are reported and minuted, with continued detriment-concern arrangements escalated to the Board committee.

checklist.step: Remediate customers affected by a defective recommendation
actions: Where a review rejection is discovered after issue, contact the customer, re-run the suitability assessment and establish whether the contract they hold is right for them.
Where it is not, offer cancellation from inception with a full premium refund plus interest, or a switch to the appropriate product at no cost to the customer.
Where an inducement was found detrimental, assess whether the affected customers paid more than they should and calculate redress on the same basis.
Record the outcome per customer and obtain Head of Compliance sign-off on the closure.
checklist.done: every affected customer is re-assessed and made whole by refund or cost-free switch, with per-customer outcomes signed off by the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Retain the review and arrangement evidence
actions: Archive each closed review with the profile, recommendation, reviewer notes, rejection trail and decision against the policy number.
Archive each inducement arrangement file with the register entry, the Art. 8(2) quality-enhancement evidence, the Art. 8(4) factor assessment and every annual re-assessment.
Apply life-of-contract plus 5 years to review records and life-of-agreement plus 5 years to arrangement files.
Confirm the arrangement files are searchable by counterparty, product and assessment year so an NCA inducement thematic can be answered without reconstruction.
checklist.done: review records and arrangement files are archived under their retention labels and the arrangement register is searchable by counterparty, product and assessment year.

testing.step: Build the population of reviews and inducement payments
actions: Extract every advised IBIP opportunity reaching issue in the quarter with policy number, adviser, product, country, review reference and review decision.
Extract from the commission platform every inducement payment made or received in the quarter with counterparty, scheme, product and amount.
Extract the inducement register and list every arrangement in force at any point in the quarter.
Reconcile the payment extract to the general ledger commission and marketing-allowance postings and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: advised IBIP issues, inducement payments and registered arrangements are extracted and the payments reconcile to the general ledger.

testing.step: Reconcile payments to assessed arrangements and issues to closed reviews
actions: Match every inducement payment to a registered arrangement with a current Art. 8 assessment on the payment date; unmatched payments are automatic fails.
Match every advised IBIP policy issued to a review record with a closed status timestamped before issue; unmatched or post-issue reviews are automatic fails.
Compare the register's annual values to actual payments per counterparty and investigate any counterparty paid materially more than its registered value.
Obtain written explanations for every unmatched item before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every payment maps to a currently assessed arrangement and every issued IBIP to a pre-issue closed review, with unmatched items explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of inducement arrangements in force and 100% of arrangements amended during the year.
Select 100% of reviews that resulted in an override, a rework closed on the same day, or an approval on the higher-paying option.
Select 30 further approved reviews at random with a seeded, reproducible draw, stratified across advisers and products.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: all arrangements plus all overrides and higher-paying-option approvals are selected alongside 30 seeded approved reviews.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 8 assessment on each sampled arrangement
actions: Read the underlying distributor agreement clauses in the contracts repository and identify the benefit terms yourself before reading the company's assessment.
Apply the Art. 8(2) quality-enhancement conditions and reach your own conclusion on whether an additional or higher-level service is genuinely funded and evidenced.
Work the Art. 8(4) factors independently, paying explicit attention to front-loaded commission and volume triggers, and compare your conclusion to the filed one.
Treat a conclusion supported only by assertion, with no measurable service evidence, as a fail even where the arrangement looks commercially normal.
testing.done: each sampled arrangement has an independent Art. 8(2) and Art. 8(4) conclusion drawn from the contract terms, with assertion-only assessments failed.

testing.step: Re-perform the suitability review on sampled recommendations
actions: Read the customer profile without the recommendation and form your own suitability view for each sampled case.
Test the recommendation against every Art. 9 element, the sustainability preference and the product target market, and reach an approve/reject conclusion of your own.
Compare to the Suitability Desk decision; any case you would have rejected that was approved is an exception, as is any approval whose recorded reasons do not cite specific profile fields.
For replacement cases recompute the switching cost against the claimed benefit over the recommended holding period and mark any switch that fails the maths.
testing.done: each sampled recommendation has an independent approve/reject conclusion, with differences from the desk decision and failed switch maths recorded as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace disclosures and suitability reports to the customer
actions: For each sampled case open the archived pack and confirm the Art. 19 nature-of-remuneration disclosure and the Art. 29 aggregated costs and charges disclosure are present as issued.
Confirm both were delivered on a durable medium before the conclusion date, using the delivery record dates.
Confirm the Art. 14 suitability report is present, names the advice given and explains how it meets the customer's preferences and objectives, rather than restating product features.
Log any pack where a document exists without delivery evidence as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled pack evidences the remuneration and costs disclosures and a substantive suitability report, all delivered on a durable medium before conclusion.

testing.step: Test the commission-scheme suspension control
actions: Confirm every active scheme in the commission platform carries an assessment reference and an expiry date on its scheme record.
In the test environment set a scheme assessment expiry into the past and attempt a payment run, confirming the payment suspends.
Review the production log of attempted payments against suspended or retired schemes and confirm none were released without Head of Compliance approval.
List any live scheme with a blank or expired assessment reference as an exception with the amounts paid under it.
testing.done: the suspension control is proven in test, production release attempts are reviewed, and any scheme paying without a current assessment is quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the review thresholds, timings and commission differentials
actions: Recompute the review-quality error rate as exceptions divided by reviews sampled and compare it to the 5% escalation threshold.
Recompute the share of approved recommendations sitting on the higher-paying option, overall and per adviser, and compare it to the figure reported to the Conduct Risk Committee.
Recompute for each sampled arrangement the days between the anniversary and the re-assessment date and count late assessments against the 30-day-before rule and the 20-business-day change rule.
Recompute the proportionality comparison on three arrangements — annual inducement value against the cost of the claimed service — and state the ratio.
testing.done: error rate, higher-paying-option share, assessment timeliness and three proportionality ratios are recomputed and compared to reported figures.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the arrangement or policy number, the counterparty or adviser, what failed and the customer or conduct impact.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — arrangement unregistered, quality-enhancement asserted not evidenced, Art. 8(4) factor skipped, review approved without field-level reasons, issue gate overridden, re-assessment late — and name an owner.
Where an inducement was paid without a current assessment, quantify the amount and refer it to the Head of Compliance for a continue-or-withdraw decision within 10 business days.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner and date, with unassessed inducement payments quantified and referred within 10 business days.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare exceptions to the zero-tolerance rules on unreviewed issues and unassessed inducements, and the 5% review-quality threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the arrangement assessments and per-case scoring behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the Suitability Desk and Distribution and approved none of the sampled items, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the unassessed-payment total and any arrangement recommended for withdrawal to the Conduct Risk Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, threshold comparisons and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the pre-solicitation gate: no producer or employee solicits an EU/EEA product until the Art. 10(2) training hours, the Annex I knowledge areas and the product-specific module are all evidenced

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 10(2) second subparagraph (minimum 15 hours professional training or development per year) with Annex I minimum professional knowledge areas, plus Art. 18 and Art. 29(1) with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 7, checked on EUR-Lex and against each national competent authority's implementing rules at the annual curriculum review

In-scope processes.value: Continuous producer readiness across every EU/EEA distribution channel plus US appointment maintenance: annual 15-hour attainment, Annex I area coverage by product type, product-specific training before any new or materially changed product is solicited, and licence/appointment currency

In-scope systems.value: Cornerstone LMS holds curricula, assignments and completion records; the Broker & Agent Portal enforces product access and NIPR holds US licence and appointment status

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Training and Competence Procedure — the curriculum map from Annex I areas to modules by product family, the 15-hour counting rules, the pre-solicitation gate, and the suspension ladder for non-completion

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution; the curriculum map is re-approved each January and immediately when a national competent authority changes its CPD rules or a new product family launches

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: 15 hours must be attained inside each calendar year per individual; product-specific training must complete before the product's first solicitation date; US appointment renewals run to each state's renewal date in NIPR and licence continuing-education deadlines follow each state's biennial cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS reminders at 1 July (mid-year hours check), 1 October, 1 November and 1 December for anyone under 15 hours; a product-launch task chain at launch minus 30, 15 and 5 business days; NIPR renewal alerts at 60 and 30 days before each state renewal date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per-individual training statements, course content versions, assessment results, and licence and appointment histories retained 5 years from the training year and for 5 years after the individual leaves the distribution role

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any solicitation by an individual without current training or a live appointment is logged with the individual, product, policies written and the disposition applied to those policies

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the reinstatement of solicitation authority after a suspension and the disposition of any business written while the individual was untrained or unappointed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every individual authorised to solicit in the period — employees, tied agents and appointed intermediaries — with their training records, and every policy they wrote, matched to their training and appointment status on the sale date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any policy solicited by an individual below the 15-hour attainment for that year, without the product module, or without a live appointment, is a fail; a curriculum coverage gap against any Annex I area is a fail at scheme level

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so the gate is monitored weekly and tested quarterly on a sample of sales, with a full annual test of 15-hour attainment across the whole population after the calendar year closes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Distribution and Learning and Development and must not administer the LMS or any curriculum under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual producer training test workpapers in the compliance evidence repository under Distribution / IDD Art. 10, cross-linked to the per-individual statements sampled

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-individual training statement showing hours, Annex I areas, course references and dates, plus the curriculum map and appointment history, producible for any named individual within 2 business days of an NCA or examiner request

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance answers NCA and state examiner questions on individual competence records; Regulatory Counsel clears any response conceding that business was solicited by an untrained or unappointed individual

checklist.step: Map the Annex I knowledge areas to curricula by product family
actions: Take the IDD Annex I areas for each distribution type — non-life (Part A), insurance-based investment products (Part B) and life other than IBIPs (Part C) — and list every area separately.

Map each area to at least one module: terms and conditions of policies offered, applicable law, claims handling, complaints handling, assessing customer needs, the insurance market, business ethics standards, financial competency and, for IBIPs, the characteristics of the product, charges, tax treatment and risk.
Mark any area with no module as a coverage gap and commission the module rather than mapping an adjacent one across it.
Add each national competent authority's own CPD conditions where they exceed the directive minimum, and note the country against the affected modules.
Obtain Head of Compliance approval of the map with a version and effective date.
checklist.done: every Annex I area for every distribution type maps to a named module, gaps are commissioned, and the map is approved with a version and effective date.

checklist.step: Define the population of individuals the 15-hour rule bites on
actions: Extract from the HRIS every employee whose role involves insurance distribution and every manager responsible for those employees, since Art. 10(2) reaches management too.
Extract from the agency management system every tied agent and appointed intermediary individual authorised to solicit.
Include contact centre agents who quote or sell, and any staff handling claims or complaints where the national rules extend the requirement to them.
Reconcile the combined list to individuals holding CRM quote authority so nobody can sell without appearing in the training population.
Refresh the population monthly and record joiners, movers and leavers with their effective dates.
checklist.done: a monthly-refreshed in-scope population reconciles to CRM quote authority and covers employees, managers, agents and selling contact centre staff.

checklist.step: Assign the annual curriculum and set the hour targets
actions: Assign each individual the curriculum for their distribution type and product families in the LMS, with a 31 December completion date for the calendar year.

Set the target at the Art. 10(2) minimum of 15 hours, raised where a national competent authority requires more, and record the applicable target on the individual's LMS profile with the country driving it.
Pro-rate the target for joiners on the national rule that applies, and record the pro-rating basis rather than silently reducing the target.
Confirm every module carries an hours value that reflects the actual learning time, since inflated hours values are the first thing an examiner tests.
Publish the assignment list to each Distribution Operations Manager so line managers own their team's attainment.
checklist.done: every individual has an assigned curriculum with a country-correct hour target, documented pro-rating for joiners and realistic module hour values.

checklist.step: Build the product-specific training before a product goes on sale
actions: Take the product approval file's target market statement, negative target market, features, charges and risks and build the module from those artefacts rather than from marketing material.
Cover explicitly what the product is not for, so the negative target market is trained rather than buried.
Include an assessment with a pass mark that requires the learner to place example customers inside or outside the target market.
Publish the module at least 15 business days before the product's first solicitation date and link it to the product record.
Version the module and force reassignment whenever the product review changes the target market or the charges.
checklist.done: a product module built from the approval file, covering the negative target market and assessed by scenario, is published 15 business days before first solicitation.

checklist.step: Gate product access on training completion
actions: Configure the Broker & Agent Portal so a product's quote and application forms are visible only to individuals whose LMS record shows the product module passed.
Configure the CRM to reject a quote for a product family where the individual's product module is incomplete, returning the module link in the rejection message.
Run a weekly reconciliation between portal entitlements and LMS completions and remove entitlements that no longer have a completion behind them.
Report weekly to the Producer Compliance Manager any individual whose entitlement was removed and any quote attempt blocked.
checklist.done: portal and CRM access to each product is entitled only by a passed module, reconciled weekly, with removals and blocked attempts reported.

checklist.step: Track hour attainment through the year rather than in December
actions: Run the LMS attainment report monthly showing hours completed year to date against target, by individual, team and country.
Issue the mid-year check on 1 July naming everyone below 7.5 hours and copy their line manager.
Issue escalating notices on 1 October, 1 November and 1 December to anyone below target, each naming the exact shortfall in hours and the modules that would close it.
Where external CPD is claimed, require the certificate with provider, date, hours and content before crediting it, and reject anything without a content description that maps to an Annex I area.
checklist.done: attainment is reported monthly with a 1 July mid-year check and escalating notices, and external CPD is credited only against an evidenced, mapped certificate.

checklist.step: Maintain licence and appointment currency for US distribution
actions: In NIPR Gateway run Appointment Renewal for each state ahead of that state's renewal date and pay the appointment fees before the deadline.
Run the Producer Database report monthly and reconcile active appointments to the producers actually writing business in each state.
Track each producer's state continuing-education status and the biennial licence renewal date, and suspend solicitation authority where a licence lapses.

For annuity products confirm the four-hour annuity training and the product-specific training required under the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model are complete before the producer solicits.
File the monthly NIPR export in the licensing evidence folder with its run date.
checklist.done: state appointments are renewed on time, monthly NIPR reconciliation matches writers to live appointments, and annuity training prerequisites are confirmed before solicitation.

checklist.step: Verify intermediary firm training where the firm trains its own people
actions: For each intermediary firm distributing the company's products, obtain the annual attestation that its relevant employees met the Art. 10(2) hours and Annex I coverage.
Require the attestation to be supported by a sample of per-individual statements rather than a bare signature, and sample five individuals per firm per year.
Confirm the firm's people who sell the company's products have completed the company's product-specific module, since the firm's own CPD does not cover it.
Suspend the firm's product access where the attestation is missing at 30 days past due and record the suspension.
checklist.done: each intermediary firm's attestation is on file with five supporting per-individual statements sampled, and product access is suspended 30 days past due.

checklist.step: Suspend solicitation authority when training lapses
actions: Apply the suspension ladder: written notice at 14 days past a deadline, product access removed at 30 days, full solicitation authority suspended at 45 days.
Remove CRM quote authority and portal entitlements at suspension and confirm the removal took effect the same day.
Notify the individual, their Distribution Operations Manager and, for intermediaries, the firm principal in writing with the exact requirement outstanding.
Record the suspension with its start date against the individual's producer record so it appears on any future examiner query.
checklist.done: the 14/30/45-day ladder is applied with access removed same-day, written notice to the individual and manager, and the suspension recorded on the producer record.

checklist.step: Reinstate authority only against evidenced completion
actions: Require the LMS completion record and, where applicable, the external CPD certificate before considering reinstatement.
Confirm licence and appointment status is live in NIPR or the relevant NCA register on the reinstatement date.
Sign the reinstatement with the date and the evidence relied on, and have entitlement restored only after the signature exists.
Record the total days suspended so repeat suspensions become visible in supervision reporting.
checklist.done: reinstatement happens only after a signed decision citing completion evidence and a live licence, with days suspended recorded.

checklist.step: Deal with business written while an individual was ineligible
actions: Run the weekly reconciliation of policies written against training and appointment status on the sale date and list every ineligible sale.
For each, review the file for customer detriment — was the demands-and-needs assessment adequate, was the product in the target market.
Where detriment is found, contact the customer, re-assess and offer cancellation with full refund or a cost-free switch.
Decide the commission treatment — commission earned on an unappointed sale is generally not payable — and instruct the Commission Analyst accordingly.
Log each case with its disposition and obtain Head of Distribution sign-off.
checklist.done: every ineligible sale is identified weekly, reviewed for detriment, remediated with the customer where needed, and its commission treatment decided and signed off.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum when rules or products change
actions: Review the curriculum map annually each January against the current Annex I text and each national competent authority's CPD conditions.
Trigger an immediate review on any product review outcome that changes a target market, on a new product launch, and on any EIOPA statement affecting distributor knowledge expectations.
Retire modules whose content is superseded and force reassignment of the replacement to everyone who took the retired version.
Record each curriculum version with its effective date so a past year's attainment can be assessed against the rules that then applied.
checklist.done: the curriculum is reviewed annually and on every product or rule change, superseded modules are retired with forced reassignment, and versions are dated.

checklist.step: Report attainment and gate performance upward
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard showing attainment against the 15-hour target by country, channel and team, product module coverage, suspensions in force and ineligible sales identified.
Report quarterly to the Conduct Risk Committee with the year-end attainment forecast and the individuals most at risk of missing it.
Escalate any team below 80% attainment at 1 October to its Distribution Operations Manager and the Head of Distribution in writing.
Include intermediary firm attestation status so third-party gaps are visible alongside internal ones.
checklist.done: monthly attainment and gate dashboards are published, quarterly committee reporting runs, and teams below 80% at 1 October are escalated in writing.

checklist.step: Produce per-individual statements ready for an examiner
actions: Generate a per-individual training statement each month showing name, role, country, hours completed year to date, target, the Annex I areas covered, and each course with its reference, date and hours.
Include product module completions with the product name and version so a product-specific question can be answered without a second query.
Export the statements into the exam evidence folder rather than relying on live LMS access under examination.
Test retrieval quarterly by picking three names at random and timing production of the full statement.
checklist.done: per-individual statements covering hours, Annex I areas, courses and product modules are exported monthly and retrieval is timed quarterly on three random names.

checklist.step: Retain training and appointment evidence
actions: Archive the annual per-individual statements, the curriculum map version, module content versions, assessment results, external CPD certificates and the monthly NIPR exports.
Apply the 5-year retention label measured from the end of the training year, extended to 5 years after the individual leaves the distribution role.
Confirm the archive is searchable by individual name, country, product and training year.
Record the archive reference against each individual's producer record.
checklist.done: training and appointment evidence is archived under a 5-year label, searchable by name, country, product and year, and referenced from the producer record.

testing.step: Build the population of solicitors and their sales
actions: Extract every individual with distribution responsibility from the HRIS and every authorised individual from the agency management system for the period, including managers responsible for distribution.
Extract every policy written in the period with the soliciting individual, product, country and sale date from the policy administration system.

Reconcile the solicitor list to individuals holding CRM quote authority and to individuals who actually wrote business; anyone writing business but absent from the training population is a population failure.
Sign the population as complete once all three lists agree.
testing.done: the solicitor population reconciles to CRM authority and to individuals who actually wrote business, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile sales to training and appointment status on the sale date
actions: Join every policy to the soliciting individual's LMS product module completion date and confirm the completion pre-dates the sale date.
Join every policy to the individual's appointment or NCA registration status on the sale date and list any sale made without a live status.
Join every policy to the individual's year-end hour attainment and list sales by anyone who finished the year below 15 hours.
List all three failure categories separately with counts and premium values, and obtain the Producer Compliance Manager's written explanation before sampling.
testing.done: every sale is joined to product module, appointment and hour-attainment status, with the three failure categories listed by count and premium.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of individuals who finished the year below the 15-hour target and 100% of individuals subject to a suspension in the period.
Select 25 individuals at random with a seeded, reproducible draw, stratified across countries, channels and intermediary firms.
Select the product modules for every product launched or materially changed in the period.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: all under-target and suspended individuals plus 25 seeded individuals and all new product modules are selected, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the hour count on each sampled individual
actions: Open each sampled individual's LMS transcript and add the hours yourself from the completed course records, ignoring the summary attainment figure.
Check each module's hours value against its actual content length and challenge any module whose stated hours plainly exceed its content.
Confirm any pro-rating for a joiner matches the documented basis and the national rule cited, and recompute it.
Confirm external CPD credits are supported by a certificate showing provider, date, hours and content mapped to an Annex I area, and strip out any credit that is not.
testing.done: hours are independently recounted per sampled individual with inflated module values challenged, pro-rating recomputed and unsupported external credits stripped.

testing.step: Test Annex I coverage against the approved curriculum map
actions: Take the Annex I areas for the individual's distribution type and confirm each maps to a module the individual actually completed in the year.
Test the curriculum map itself: any Annex I area with no module, or covered only by an adjacent module, is a scheme-level fail affecting everyone on that curriculum.
Confirm the curriculum version in force on each completion date is the version whose coverage you are testing, not the current one.
Confirm IBIP distributors completed the Part B areas covering product characteristics, charges, tax treatment and risk.
testing.done: each sampled individual's completions cover every applicable Annex I area under the curriculum version then in force, with map gaps raised as scheme-level fails.

testing.step: Trace product modules and portal entitlements to the sale
actions: For each sampled new or changed product, confirm the module was published at least 15 business days before the first recorded solicitation date.
Confirm the module content came from the product approval file by comparing its target market and charges content to the approved statement.
In the Broker & Agent Portal confirm the product's forms are entitled only to individuals with a passed module, by attempting access with a test account lacking the completion.
Trace ten sales of each sampled product to the soliciting individual's completion date and confirm each completion pre-dates the sale.
testing.done: each product module is proven published 15 business days ahead, sourced from the approval file, entitlement-gated in test, and pre-dating ten traced sales.

testing.step: Re-run the licensing and appointment reconciliation independently
actions: Run the NIPR Producer Database report yourself for three sampled states and compare it to the copy held in the licensing evidence folder.
Confirm appointment renewal was completed before each state's renewal date and count any appointment renewed late or lapsed.

For annuity sales confirm the four-hour annuity training and the product-specific training required by the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model completed before the first annuity solicitation by that producer.
For EU/EEA individuals confirm the registration entry with the relevant national competent authority is live on the sale date.
testing.done: appointment and registration status is independently re-run for three states and all sampled EU individuals, with late or lapsed renewals counted.

testing.step: Test the suspension ladder and recompute its timings
actions: For each sampled suspension recompute the 14, 30 and 45-day dates from the missed deadline and compare them to when notice, access removal and suspension actually happened.
Confirm CRM quote authority and portal entitlement were removed on the same day the suspension was recorded, using the system audit trail.
Confirm no policy was written by the individual between the suspension date and the signed reinstatement date.
Confirm each reinstatement carries a Head of Distribution signature citing the completion evidence and a live licence on that date.
testing.done: suspension timings are recomputed against actual actions, same-day access removal is evidenced, and no sales occur inside any suspension window.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the individual, country, product, policies affected and the premium involved.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — curriculum gap, inflated module hours, entitlement not revoked, joiner never added to the population, external CPD credited without evidence, appointment renewal missed — and name an owner.
For every sale by an untrained or unappointed individual, open a customer detriment review and record the commission treatment decision.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner and date, with ineligible sales driving a detriment review and a commission treatment decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare exceptions to the zero-tolerance rules on sales by under-trained, unmodulated or unappointed individuals and to the scheme-level Annex I coverage rule.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the recounted transcripts and curriculum map testing behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution and Learning and Development and administers no curriculum under test, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, ineligible-sale premium totals and any curriculum coverage gap to the Conduct Risk Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, ineligible-sale totals and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Accountable that every EU/EEA customer receives the full pre-contract disclosure set on a durable medium before the contract concludes, in every channel including telephone and digital

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 20(1) on demands and needs, Art. 20(5) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 for the Insurance Product Information Document, Arts. 18 and 19 on distributor and remuneration disclosure, Art. 23 on the durable medium and paper default, and Art. 29(1) for IBIP costs and charges, verified on EUR-Lex at each template revision

In-scope processes.value: Pre-contract disclosure delivery on every EU/EEA new business sale and every mid-term variation that changes cover, across tied agents, brokers, bancassurance, telephone and digital self-service

In-scope systems.value: Document generation and delivery orchestrated from the policy administration system, with delivery receipts written back to the CRM opportunity and the archived pack held in the document repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Pre-Contract Disclosure Procedure — the document set per product family and country, the IPID content and format rules, the durable medium and paper-default rules, the timing rule against conclusion, and the failure-handling routine

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; the document set and templates are re-approved annually and immediately on any product change, national language requirement change or Implementing Regulation update

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per sale — every document must be delivered in good time before conclusion, meaning before the customer is bound; for distance telephone sales concluded at the customer's request the pack follows immediately after conclusion on a durable medium and the customer is told this before agreeing

Deadline reminders configured.value: The policy administration system blocks conclusion where a required document has no delivery record, and raises a task to the adviser and supervisor when a delivery record is unconfirmed after 24 hours or a paper pack is unreturned after 5 business days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The exact document versions delivered, the delivery receipt with date, channel and medium, and any customer durable-medium consent retained for the life of the contract plus 5 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any contract concluded without a complete delivered disclosure set is logged with policy number, missing document, channel and the customer remedy applied, including any re-opened withdrawal period

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the remedy on every missing-disclosure case — re-issue with a fresh withdrawal period, or cancellation from inception with full refund where the customer would not have bought
