checklist.step: Define the required document set per product family and country
actions: For each product family list every pre-contract document: the Insurance Product Information Document for non-life under Art. 20(5), the demands-and-needs statement, the Art. 18 distributor information, the Art. 19 nature-of-remuneration statement, the policy wording or specimen, and for IBIPs the PRIIPs key information document and the Art. 29(1) aggregated costs and charges disclosure.
Add country-specific documents each national competent authority requires beyond the directive and note the country against each.
Record the language rules per country, including where the customer may choose a language and where the local official language is mandatory.
Record for each document the delivery timing rule — before conclusion, in good time before conclusion, or immediately after for a customer-requested telephone conclusion.
Obtain Head of Compliance approval with a version and effective date.
checklist.done: an approved, version-dated document set exists per product family and country with language rules and per-document timing rules recorded.

checklist.step: Build the IPID to the implementing regulation format
actions: Draft the IPID to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469: short, standalone, A4, in the prescribed order with the prescribed headings and icons for what is insured, what is not insured, restrictions, where and when cover applies, obligations, payment, start and end of cover, and how to cancel.
Keep it to two sides of A4 in normal circumstances and never exceed three, and use plain language a non-specialist can read at a single sitting.
Confirm the content agrees with the policy wording clause by clause — an IPID that flatters the cover is a mis-selling exposure, not a marketing asset.
Have the product owner and Regulatory Counsel approve the draft, then version it with an effective date.
Produce the approved translations for every country of sale and have each checked by a local reviewer, not machine translation alone.
checklist.done: the IPID follows the implementing regulation's format and length, agrees with the wording clause by clause, is counsel-approved, versioned and locally checked in every language.

checklist.step: Build the Art. 18 and Art. 19 disclosure content
actions: Draft the Art. 18 statement giving the distributor's identity and address, whether it is an intermediary or an undertaking, the register in which it is entered and how that entry can be verified, and the complaints and out-of-court redress routes available.

Draft the Art. 19 statement giving the nature of the remuneration received — fee paid by the customer, commission included in the premium, another kind of remuneration, or a combination — for the specific contract.

For intermediaries add the Art. 19(1) statements on whether advice is given on a fair and personal analysis, whether there is a contractual obligation to place with one or more undertakings, and the names of those undertakings on request.
Confirm the wording states the correct out-of-court redress body for the customer's country — the national ombudsman or FIN-NET member — not a generic reference.
checklist.done: Art. 18 and Art. 19 statements are drafted with register verification, remuneration nature, analysis basis and the correct country-specific redress body named.

checklist.step: Wire the document set into generation and delivery
actions: Configure the document generation rules so the approved set for the product family and country is assembled automatically at quote, using the template version live on that date.
Write the delivery record back to the CRM opportunity with document name, template version, delivery date and time, medium and channel.
Block the conclusion step where any required document has no confirmed delivery record, with no operator-level override.
Confirm the version stamp is captured on the delivered PDF itself so a reprint years later cannot silently substitute a newer template.
Test the rules against scripted scenarios per country and product family and retain the test evidence with the release note.
checklist.done: documents generate from the version live at quote, delivery records write back with version and timestamp, and conclusion is blocked without them.

checklist.step: Deliver on the right durable medium with paper as the default
actions: Default to paper as Art. 23(2) requires, and use another durable medium or a website only where the customer has chosen it and the Art. 23(4) and 23(5) conditions are met.
Where a durable medium other than paper is used, record the customer's choice and confirm the medium is appropriate to the business conducted with them.

Where a website is used, record that the customer was notified electronically of the address and the place on the site where the document can be accessed, and that it stays accessible for as long as the customer reasonably needs it.
Tell the customer they may request a paper copy free of charge and record that this was said.
checklist.done: paper is the default, any alternative medium or website use is evidenced against the Art. 23 conditions, and the free paper-copy right is recorded as communicated.

checklist.step: Handle telephone sales under the distance rules
actions: Confirm the telephone script gives the Art. 21 reduced information set by voice before conclusion and tells the customer the full pack follows immediately after on a durable medium.
Confirm the customer's agreement to conclude on that basis is captured on the recording and referenced on the opportunity.
Confirm the full pack issues automatically within one business day of conclusion and that the delivery record is written back.
Sample five calls per agent per month against these points and coach any agent concluding without the voice disclosure or the customer's agreement.
checklist.done: telephone sales evidence the voice disclosure, the customer's recorded agreement and full-pack delivery within one business day, with five calls per agent reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Handle the digital self-service journey
actions: Confirm the journey presents the IPID, demands-and-needs statement and Art. 18/19 disclosures before the payment step and not behind a link the customer can skip.
Confirm the customer must actively acknowledge receipt and that the acknowledgement writes a delivery record with timestamp and template version.
Confirm the documents are downloadable and emailed to the customer, and that the customer can request paper free of charge from the confirmation screen.
Test the journey on mobile as well as desktop, since a document that renders unreadably on a phone has not been effectively delivered.
checklist.done: the digital journey presents all documents before payment with an acknowledged, timestamped delivery record, a free paper route and a verified mobile rendering.

checklist.step: Deliver the IBIP costs and charges disclosure
actions: For every IBIP deliver the Art. 29(1) information: all costs and related charges aggregated, including third-party payments, so the customer can see the cumulative effect on the return.
Deliver the PRIIPs key information document under Regulation (EU) 1286/2014 in good time before the customer is bound, and record the delivery separately from the IPID.
Where a periodic cost disclosure is due during the contract, schedule it so the annual statement carries the actual costs incurred.
Confirm the illustrated charges in the disclosure reconcile to the charges configured on the product in the administration system.
checklist.done: every IBIP evidences an aggregated costs and charges disclosure and a pre-conclusion PRIIPs KID, with illustrated charges reconciled to configured product charges.

checklist.step: Handle cross-selling and ancillary product disclosure
actions: Where insurance is offered with another good or service, confirm the customer is told whether the components can be bought separately and given a separate description and separate cost for each, as Art. 24(1) requires.
Where insurance is ancillary to a non-insurance good or service, confirm the customer is offered the option of buying the good or service separately, unless the exemption applies.
Confirm the demands-and-needs assessment covers the package as a whole rather than only the primary product.
Block any bundled journey that presents a single combined price with no component breakdown.
checklist.done: every cross-sold package evidences separate component descriptions and costs, a separate-purchase option where required, and a package-level needs assessment.

checklist.step: Monitor delivery completeness daily
actions: Run the daily exception report listing contracts concluded in the last 24 hours where any required document has no delivery record or has one timestamped at or after conclusion.
Investigate each case the same day, identify whether the cause is a generation failure, a delivery failure or a sequence failure, and record it.
Escalate generation or template failures to the document generation team as a production incident, since they usually affect many contracts rather than one.
Report the daily count and cause split to the Distribution Operations Manager and weekly to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: a daily exception report is worked to cause the same day, with template and generation failures escalated as production incidents and counts reported weekly.

checklist.step: Remedy the customer where a disclosure was missed
actions: For each missed disclosure, deliver the document immediately on a durable medium with a covering explanation.
Reopen the statutory withdrawal or cooling-off period from the date of correct delivery where national law requires it, and tell the customer their rights in the covering letter.
Where the missing document would plausibly have changed the decision — an IPID misdescribing an exclusion, an undisclosed charge — offer cancellation from inception with a full refund.
Record the remedy per customer and sign the case closed.
checklist.done: each missed disclosure is corrected on a durable medium with the withdrawal period reopened where required and cancellation offered where the decision could have changed.

checklist.step: Keep the template library current and withdraw superseded versions
actions: Hold every template version with its approval signature, effective date and withdrawal date, and never overwrite a version in place.
On any product change, wording change or regulatory change, produce a new version and set the old one to withdrawn with a date rather than deleting it.
Confirm the generation system points at the current version in every country on the effective date, and run a post-release check on the first ten documents produced.
Retain withdrawn versions so a document delivered three years ago can be reproduced exactly as the customer received it.
checklist.done: the library holds every version with approval, effective and withdrawal dates, generation points at the current version, and withdrawn versions remain reproducible.

checklist.step: Review IPID content against the wording annually
actions: Each year, and on any wording change, compare each IPID line by line to the current policy wording covering insured perils, exclusions, limits, excesses, territorial scope and cancellation rights.
Correct any statement the wording does not support and treat an overstated cover description as an urgent fix, not an annual-cycle item.
Confirm the document still fits the format, order and length the implementing regulation prescribes after the edits.
Re-approve, version and republish, and force the generation system onto the new version on its effective date.
checklist.done: every IPID is reconciled line by line to the current wording annually and on change, corrected, re-approved, versioned and republished.

checklist.step: Report delivery performance and content quality
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard showing delivery completeness by product, country and channel, the pre-conclusion timing rate, the cause split for failures and the count of reopened withdrawal periods.
Report quarterly to the Conduct Risk Committee alongside the complaint root causes tagged to disclosure, so content failures and complaint patterns are read together.
Escalate any channel below 99.5% delivery completeness in a month in writing to its Distribution Operations Manager.
Include cross-sold packages as a separate line, since bundle journeys fail differently from single-product ones.
checklist.done: monthly delivery and content dashboards are published with quarterly committee reporting and written escalation below 99.5% completeness.

checklist.step: Retain the delivered pack per policy
actions: Archive against each policy number the exact documents delivered, their template versions, the delivery receipts with date, time, medium and channel, and any durable-medium consent.
Apply the life-of-contract plus 5 years retention label and extend automatically where a complaint or ombudsman case cites the policy.
Confirm retrieval by policy number returns the pack as the customer received it within 2 business days, testing five random policies each quarter.
Record the retrieval test result in the Distribution evidence folder.
checklist.done: per-policy delivered packs with versions and receipts are archived under a life-plus-5-years label with a quarterly five-policy 2-day retrieval test.

testing.step: Build the population of contracts concluded in the quarter
actions: Extract every EU/EEA contract concluded in the quarter with policy number, product, country, channel, conclusion timestamp and adviser or agent identifier.
Add mid-term variations that changed cover, since these carry their own disclosure obligation and are routinely omitted from disclosure testing.
Reconcile the count and premium to the new business figures in the quarter-end management accounts and explain differences.
Confirm digital self-service and telephone sales are included and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: an all-channel population including mid-term variations is extracted, reconciled to management accounts and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to delivery records document by document
actions: For each contract list the documents the approved set requires for its product family and country as at the conclusion date.
Match each required document to a delivery record and list every missing one by document type.
Compare each delivery timestamp to the conclusion timestamp and list every delivery at or after conclusion, other than telephone sales with a recorded customer agreement.
Obtain the Distribution Operations Manager's written explanation of each gap before sampling.
testing.done: every contract is reconciled document by document with missing deliveries and post-conclusion timings listed and explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Select 100% of products whose IPID or disclosure template changed in the quarter, and 100% of cross-sold packages.
Select 40 contracts at random with a seeded, reproducible draw, stratified so every country, channel and product family is represented.
Add 10 telephone-concluded and 10 digital self-service contracts specifically, since their delivery mechanics differ.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all changed templates and cross-sold packages plus 40 stratified and 20 channel-specific contracts, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the IPID content check against the wording
actions: Open the delivered IPID version for each sampled contract and the policy wording in force at conclusion.
Check line by line that insured perils, exclusions, limits, excesses, territorial scope, obligations, premium payment terms, contract start and end and cancellation rights all agree with the wording.
Check the format against Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469: prescribed order, prescribed headings, icons, length within two sides (never beyond three) and plain language.
Treat any statement the wording does not support as an exception and mark overstatement of cover as high severity.
testing.done: each sampled IPID is checked line by line against the in-force wording and against the implementing regulation format, with overstatements marked high severity.

testing.step: Trace the delivered pack to the customer with medium and timing
actions: Open the archived pack for each sampled contract and confirm the documents present match the required set and the template versions live at conclusion.
Confirm each delivery record states the medium and that paper was used unless a recorded customer choice supports another durable medium under Art. 23.
Where a website was used, confirm the electronic notification of the address and location was recorded and that the document remains accessible.
Confirm each delivery pre-dates conclusion, and for telephone sales confirm the recorded customer agreement and full-pack issue within one business day.
testing.done: each sampled pack is traced to correct versions, an evidenced durable medium and a pre-conclusion delivery, with telephone exceptions properly evidenced.

testing.step: Test the IBIP costs, PRIIPs and cross-selling disclosures
actions: For each sampled IBIP confirm the Art. 29(1) aggregated costs and charges disclosure was delivered and shows the cumulative effect on the return, including third-party payments.
Confirm the PRIIPs key information document was delivered in good time before the customer was bound and recompute the reduction-in-yield figure against the product's configured charges.
For each sampled cross-sold package confirm separate descriptions and separate costs per component and the option to buy separately where Art. 24 requires it.
Confirm the demands-and-needs assessment addressed the package as a whole.
testing.done: IBIP costs and PRIIPs disclosures are verified and recomputed, and every cross-sold package evidences component pricing and a package-level needs assessment.

testing.step: Test the conclusion block by attempting to defeat it
actions: In the test environment attempt to conclude a contract with one required document missing a delivery record and confirm the block fires.
Attempt to conclude with a delivery record timestamped after the proposed conclusion time and confirm the block fires.
Attempt to generate a document for a back-dated quote and confirm the system selects the template version live on the quote date, not the current one.
Review the production override log and confirm every override carries an approver identity and a written reason.
testing.done: all three system controls are proven by attempted circumvention in test and every production override is evidenced with an approver and reason.

testing.step: Recompute completeness, timing and reopened-period arithmetic
actions: Recompute delivery completeness as contracts with a full delivered set divided by contracts concluded, overall and by channel, and compare to the 99.5% escalation threshold.
Recompute the IPID content error rate as failed IPIDs divided by IPIDs reviewed and compare to the 1% threshold.
For each missed disclosure recompute the reopened withdrawal period end date from the corrected delivery date under the applicable national rule and confirm the customer was told the correct date.
Extrapolate the sampled content error rate over the population and state the estimated number of customers who received a defective document.
testing.done: completeness, content error rate and reopened withdrawal dates are recomputed against thresholds with population impact extrapolated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording policy number, country, channel, the document that failed and whether the failure was absence, timing, medium or content.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — template not updated after a wording change, generation rule missing a country document, delivery receipt not written back, website medium used without customer choice, bundle journey with combined pricing — and name an owner.
For content failures affecting a template, quantify every contract issued on that version and open a population-level remediation rather than fixing single files.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner and date, with template content failures escalated to population-level remediation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance absence and timing rules and the 1% IPID content threshold, and state whether each was breached.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the per-contract tracing and IPID scoring behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution and the document generation team and approved none of the sampled templates, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, extrapolated customer impact and any reopened withdrawal periods to the Conduct Risk Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, threshold comparisons and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly second-line sales supervision programme — file review, call listening and mystery shopping — that evidences distribution is carried out honestly, fairly and professionally in the customer's best interest

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17(1) as the standard tested, Art. 30(3) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 16 for the appropriateness and record-keeping expectations, and Art. 29(2) with Arts. 8-9 of that regulation where an inducement sits behind the sale, re-read at each annual programme design

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly risk-based supervision of completed EU/EEA sales across every channel: advised and non-advised, tied and intermediated, telephone, face-to-face and digital, covering file quality, sales conversation conduct and outcome indicators

In-scope systems.value: Sales files reviewed on the CRM opportunity with call recordings retrieved from the contact centre platform and outcomes recorded in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Sales Supervision Procedure — the risk model that targets the sample, the scoring sheet with its attributes and weightings, the call listening protocol, the mystery shopping design and the consequence framework for adviser scores

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Conduct Risk Committee; the risk model and scoring sheet are re-approved annually and after any thematic finding that shows the model missed a risk

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Sample drawn within 10 business days of quarter-end, reviews completed within 30 business days, adviser feedback issued within 5 business days of each review, and the quarterly supervision report to the Conduct Risk Committee within 45 business days of quarter-end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Programme tasks at quarter-end +10 (sample drawn), +30 (reviews complete), +40 (report drafted), +45 (committee submission), with reviewer-level ageing alerts at 5 and 10 days on any unreviewed file

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Sampling methodology, per-file scoring sheets, call listening notes, mystery shopping reports, adviser feedback and the quarterly report retained 5 years from the report date, and for the life of the contract plus 5 years where a file drove a customer remedy

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each failed file is logged with adviser, intermediary code, product, the failed attribute, the customer impact and the disposition — coaching, supervision, customer remedy or referral

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every adviser placed under enhanced supervision or removed from solicitation, and every population-level remediation triggered by a systemic finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All EU/EEA sales completed in the quarter as the sampling frame, plus the supervision programme's own outputs — the drawn sample, scoring sheets, call reviews, mystery shops and adviser feedback records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A file fails on any critical attribute — no demands-and-needs basis, sale into the negative target market, disclosure not delivered before conclusion, or a recommendation contradicted by the recorded profile; an adviser above a 10% critical-fail rate goes to enhanced supervision and above 20% is removed from solicitation pending review

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Supervision runs quarterly; the independent test of the supervision programme runs quarterly on the just-closed cycle, with an annual assessment of whether the risk model is still selecting the right files

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance Monitoring and Distribution and must not have scored any file in the cycle under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly supervision programme test workpaper — sampling reconstruction, re-scored files, call re-listening notes, exception list — in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Sales Supervision

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Methodology, four quarters of samples and scoring sheets, adviser outcome history and the consequence decisions, producible as an Art. 17(1) supervision evidence pack within 10 business days of an NCA or examiner request

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the supervision evidence response; Regulatory Counsel clears any disclosure of adviser-level failure rates or any admission of a systemic sales practice issue before it is filed

checklist.step: Design the risk model that targets the quarterly sample
actions: Build the risk score per adviser and per intermediary from the conduct metrics: complaint rate, cooling-off cancellation rate, 13-month lapse rate, replacement rate, declined-profile-field rate, higher-paying-option share and prior review failure rate.
Weight new advisers, advisers back from suspension and advisers who joined from a firm with a known conduct history to the top of the sample regardless of their own numbers.
Add product risk: insurance-based investment products, long-term protection with medical underwriting, and any product whose review found a target-market mismatch.
Add vulnerability indicators — customer age, health disclosures, first-time buyers — since these drive the greatest potential harm.
Obtain Head of Compliance approval of the model and record the version and effective date.
checklist.done: an approved, version-dated risk model scores advisers, intermediaries, products and customer vulnerability and drives the sample.

checklist.step: Draw the quarterly sample and document the method
actions: Extract the sales population for the quarter from the warehouse by adviser, intermediary, product, country, channel and customer indicators.
Draw the sample within 10 business days of quarter-end: every adviser gets a minimum of three files, high-risk advisers get ten, and every product family and country is represented.
Add a random component drawn on a recorded seed so the programme is not fully predictable to advisers.
Record the population size, the risk model version, the seed, the strata and the draw date in the sampling workpaper.
Publish the sample to reviewers without telling advisers which of their files were drawn.
checklist.done: the sample is drawn within 10 business days with a recorded seed, model version and strata, giving every adviser at least three files.

checklist.step: Score each sampled file against the standard attributes
actions: Open the CRM opportunity and score the file on the approved sheet: demands-and-needs captured before product selection, answers specific to the customer, existing cover recorded, target-market fit, disclosure delivered before conclusion, recommendation reasoned against profile fields, and affordability considered.
Mark the four critical attributes separately, since any one of them failing fails the file regardless of the total score.
Read the adviser's own notes for language suggesting pressure, urgency or a promised outcome the policy does not deliver.
Record the score, the failed attributes and the evidence reference for each finding on the scoring sheet.
Never score a file you supervised, sold or coached — reassign it to another reviewer.
checklist.done: each sampled file carries a completed scoring sheet with critical attributes marked separately and evidence references for every finding.

checklist.step: Listen to the sales conversation where one was recorded
actions: Retrieve the recording using the reference on the opportunity and listen to the whole sales conversation, not only the compliance script at the end.
Check the demands-and-needs questions came before the product was named and that the customer's answers, not the adviser's suggestions, drove the recommendation.
Check the required disclosures were given by voice where the sale concluded on the call, and that exclusions were stated as plainly as benefits.
Note any pressure language — limited-time framing, discouraging the customer from taking time, talking over a stated concern — with the timestamp.
Attach the listening note with timestamps to the scoring sheet.
checklist.done: each recorded sale has a full-call listening note with timestamps covering question sequence, disclosure delivery and any pressure language.

checklist.step: Run mystery shopping across the highest-risk journeys
actions: Design at least four scenarios per quarter, including one where the shopper's stated needs make the flagship product unsuitable and one where the shopper presents a vulnerability indicator.
Run the shops across every channel — branch or agent, telephone and digital — using an external provider so shoppers are not recognisable.

Score against the same attributes as file review plus conversation-specific ones: was advice offered or pushed, was the negative target market respected, were charges volunteered or only disclosed on request.
Feed shop findings into the same exception log as file review so a channel weakness shows up once, not twice.
Report shop results to the Conduct Risk Committee separately, since they measure behaviour the file never records.
checklist.done: at least four scenarios per quarter are shopped across all channels with results scored on the common attributes and reported separately to the committee.

checklist.step: Test outcomes rather than only process
actions: For each sampled file check what happened to the customer afterwards: did the policy lapse inside 13 months, was it cancelled in the cooling-off period, did the customer complain, was a claim declined on a term the file never explained.
Where a poor outcome followed a file that scored well, re-read the file — a clean process producing a bad outcome usually means the scoring sheet is missing an attribute.
Where the outcome shows the customer did not understand what they bought, log it as a comprehension failure even where every document was delivered.
Feed attribute gaps back into the scoring sheet at the annual review.
checklist.done: each sampled file is checked against the customer's subsequent outcome, with clean files producing bad outcomes re-read and scoring gaps captured.

checklist.step: Give the adviser specific, evidenced feedback within five days
actions: Issue the scoring sheet to the adviser and their line manager within five business days of the review, naming the file, the attribute and the evidence.
Hold a documented conversation on every failed file rather than sending the sheet and moving on.
Agree specific corrective behaviour with a date and record it on the adviser's supervision record.
Allow the adviser to challenge a finding in writing within five business days and have a second reviewer decide the challenge.
checklist.done: feedback issues within five business days with a documented conversation, agreed corrective behaviour and a challenge route decided by a second reviewer.

checklist.step: Apply the consequence framework to persistent failure
actions: Compute each adviser's critical-fail rate for the quarter and compare it to the 10% enhanced supervision and 20% removal thresholds.
Place advisers above 10% under enhanced supervision: 100% pre-issue file checking for the next quarter and a re-training assignment.
Remove advisers above 20% from solicitation pending a full review of their in-force book, and record the removal on the producer record.
Where the adviser is an intermediary firm's employee, notify the firm principal in writing and require the firm's own action plan.
Report every consequence decision to the Head of Compliance for sign-off.
checklist.done: critical-fail rates drive enhanced supervision above 10% and removal above 20%, with firm notification and Head of Compliance sign-off recorded.

checklist.step: Review the whole book where an adviser fails badly
actions: Where an adviser is removed or shows a systemic failure pattern, extract every policy they wrote over the period the behaviour existed, not just the review quarter.
Review the full book against the critical attributes and identify customers who may have been harmed.
Contact affected customers, re-assess their needs and offer the appropriate remedy — correction, cancellation with refund, or a cost-free switch.
Record the book review scope, findings and remedies and have the Head of Compliance sign the closure.
checklist.done: a failed adviser's full book over the behaviour period is reviewed, affected customers are contacted and remedied, and the closure is signed.

checklist.step: Escalate systemic findings to product and process owners
actions: Group failures by attribute, product, channel and country to separate individual adviser failure from a systemic design problem.
Where a product fails across many advisers, refer it to the Art. 25 product review rather than treating it as a training issue.

Where a channel journey fails structurally — a digital step that lets the customer skip a document, a script that names the product first — raise it as a process change with the channel owner and a due date.
Track systemic referrals separately in the quarterly report so they are not lost among individual coaching actions.
checklist.done: failures are grouped to separate individual from systemic causes, with product referrals into the Art. 25 review and channel fixes raised with owners and due dates.

checklist.step: Log every failed file with a disposition
actions: Raise one GRC issue per failed file recording policy number, adviser, intermediary code, product, country, the failed attribute and the customer impact.
Set the disposition — coaching, enhanced supervision, customer remedy, book review, systemic referral — with an owner and a due date.
Link the issue to the scoring sheet and, where relevant, the call listening note so the evidence travels with the record.
Close only against evidence: a coaching record, a completed remedy, or a re-review of the adviser's later files.
checklist.done: every failed file has a linked GRC issue with a disposition, owner, due date and evidence-based closure rule.

checklist.step: Report the quarterly supervision results
actions: Submit the quarterly supervision report to the Conduct Risk Committee within 45 business days of quarter-end covering files reviewed, pass rate, critical-fail rate by adviser, channel and product, mystery shop results and systemic referrals.
State the Art. 17(1) conclusion plainly: whether the evidence shows distribution acting in customers' best interests, with the failures that qualify it.
Escalate any channel or product with a critical-fail rate above 10% and any adviser removed from solicitation.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute the decisions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: the quarterly report is submitted within 45 business days with a stated Art. 17(1) conclusion and minuted decisions on every escalation.

checklist.step: Re-review previously failed advisers in the following cycle
actions: Carry every adviser who failed in the quarter into the next quarter's sample at the enhanced volume, regardless of what the risk model says.
Compare their new critical-fail rate to the prior quarter and record whether the coaching worked.
Where the rate has not improved, escalate one step up the consequence framework rather than repeating the same coaching.
Record the re-review outcome against the original GRC issue before closing it.
checklist.done: every previously failed adviser is re-reviewed at enhanced volume with the change in critical-fail rate recorded and escalation applied where it did not improve.

checklist.step: Reassess the risk model annually against what it missed
actions: Each year compare the advisers who generated complaints, ombudsman cases and poor outcomes against the risk scores the model gave them beforehand.
Where the model failed to flag an adviser who later caused harm, identify the missing input and add it.
Re-weight inputs that produced no discriminating power and remove them rather than carrying dead weight.
Re-approve the model with a new version and effective date and record the back-test evidence behind the change.
checklist.done: the risk model is back-tested annually against realised harm, re-weighted, re-approved and version-dated with the back-test evidence retained.

checklist.step: Retain the supervision evidence
actions: Archive the sampling workpaper, scoring sheets, call listening notes, mystery shop reports, adviser feedback records and the quarterly report under Market Conduct / Sales Supervision / <year>-Q<n>.
Apply the 5-year retention label from the report date, extended to life-of-contract plus 5 years where a file drove a customer remedy.
Confirm the archive is searchable by adviser, intermediary, product, country and attribute so an NCA question about one adviser can be answered directly.
Record the archive reference on each GRC issue raised in the cycle.
checklist.done: the supervision cycle is archived under its retention labels, searchable by adviser and attribute, and referenced from every GRC issue.

testing.step: Rebuild the sampling frame for the quarter
actions: Extract the full EU/EEA sales population for the quarter yourself with adviser, intermediary, product, country, channel and customer indicators.
Compare your population to the frame the programme used and list any adviser, channel or country excluded from the frame.
Confirm digital self-service and telephone sales were in the frame, since automated channels are commonly left out of file review.
Sign the frame reconciliation before assessing the sample.
testing.done: an independent sampling frame is built and reconciled to the programme's frame, with any excluded adviser, channel or country listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the drawn sample to the approved methodology
actions: Read the approved risk model version and recompute the risk scores for a subset of advisers from the underlying conduct metrics.
Confirm the sample gives every adviser at least three files and every high-risk adviser ten, and that every product family and country is represented.
Re-draw the random component using the recorded seed and confirm it reproduces the same files.
List any adviser with sales in the quarter and no file reviewed as an exception.
testing.done: risk scores are recomputed, minimum coverage is verified, the seeded draw is reproduced and unreviewed advisers are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the test sample of reviews
actions: Select 100% of files scored as passes for advisers whose customers later complained or lapsed inside 13 months.
Select 100% of files where a critical attribute was marked failed, to test that the disposition matched the failure.
Select 25 further scored files at random with a seeded draw, stratified across reviewers so reviewer bias is testable.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the test sample covers all critical-fail files, all passes followed by poor outcomes and 25 seeded files stratified by reviewer.

testing.step: Re-score the sampled files independently
actions: Open each sampled file and score it on the approved sheet without reading the original score first.
Compare your score to the recorded one attribute by attribute and record every difference, particularly on the four critical attributes.
Treat a pass on a file you would fail on a critical attribute as a supervision failure, since the programme is meant to catch exactly that.
Compute the disagreement rate per reviewer to expose whether one reviewer is systematically lenient.
testing.done: each sampled file is independently re-scored with attribute-level differences recorded and a per-reviewer disagreement rate computed.

testing.step: Re-listen to sampled call recordings
actions: Retrieve the recording for ten sampled files and listen to the full conversation rather than the compliance close.
Confirm the reviewer's listening note reflects what is on the recording, including any pressure language, and check the timestamps cited.
Confirm the demands-and-needs questions preceded the product being named and that exclusions were stated as plainly as benefits.
Log any recording that is missing, truncated or unretrievable as a control exception, since an unrecorded sale cannot be supervised.
testing.done: ten recordings are re-listened against the reviewer notes with timestamps verified and missing or truncated recordings logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Test the mystery shopping programme for independence and coverage
actions: Confirm at least four scenarios ran in the quarter, including an unsuitable-need scenario and a vulnerability scenario, across all channels.
Confirm the provider is external and that shopper identities were not disclosable to the branches or advisers shopped.
Read the shop reports and confirm the findings were scored on the same attributes as file review and fed into the same exception log.
Confirm no shop finding was closed without an owner and a due date.
testing.done: mystery shopping coverage, independence, common scoring and exception-log integration are all verified for the quarter.

testing.step: Trace dispositions and consequences to evidence
actions: For each critical-fail file confirm a GRC issue exists with a disposition, owner and due date, linked to the scoring sheet.
Confirm feedback reached the adviser within five business days by checking the feedback record date against the review date.
Confirm every adviser above the 10% threshold was placed under enhanced supervision and every adviser above 20% removed, with entitlements actually withdrawn in the producer system.
Where a book review was required, confirm its scope covered the full behaviour period and that affected customers were contacted.
testing.done: every critical-fail file traces to a disposed issue, timely feedback, an applied consequence with withdrawn entitlements, and a scoped book review where required.

testing.step: Recompute the rates, thresholds and programme deadlines
actions: Recompute the overall pass rate and each adviser's critical-fail rate from the scoring sheets and compare to the published figures and the 10% and 20% thresholds.
Recompute your own re-score disagreement rate and state whether the programme's own results understate the failure level.
Recompute the programme deadlines — sample by quarter-end +10, reviews by +30, report by +45 — against the actual dates and count late days.
Extrapolate your re-scored critical-fail rate across the population and state the estimated number of customers on defective sales.
testing.done: pass and critical-fail rates, reviewer disagreement and all three programme deadlines are recomputed, with population impact extrapolated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the file or programme element, the adviser or reviewer involved, what failed and the conduct exposure created.

Assign a root cause from the standing list — frame excluded a channel, sample below minimum coverage, reviewer leniency, feedback late, consequence not applied, recording unavailable, systemic finding not referred — and name an owner.
Where reviewer leniency is evidenced, require re-scoring of that reviewer's whole quarter rather than only the sampled files.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, with evidenced reviewer leniency triggering a full re-score of that reviewer's quarter.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the recomputed critical-fail rates and reviewer disagreement to the programme's published conclusion and state whether the programme understated the position.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the re-scored files, re-listened calls and recomputed thresholds behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance Monitoring and Distribution and scored no file in the cycle, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, extrapolated customer impact and any adviser or product escalation to the Conduct Risk Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed, dated workpaper with a stated conclusion, recomputed rates and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
